title: Echelon hifigan support
author: echelon
body:
This is a fairly large feature that is 80% complete (and usable) on the backend:

- Database schema for custom vocoders and "generic downloader jobs"
- A new job runner for "generic downloads", which will be easy to repurpose for other things in the future
- CRUD endpoints for creating generic download jobs and checking their statuses
- Custom vocoders are the first type of "generic download"
- Some (but not all) of the CRUD endpoints for querying custom vocoders
- Updates to existing endpoints to allow modifying TTS synthesizers to include custom vocoders, return info on them, etc.
- Updates to inference job to download and then send python the new custom vocoder

This does not include the follow-up codegen for offline sqlx tests/build.

title: Do not respawn SadTalker jobs when face detection fails
author: echelon
body:
Currently SadTalker jobs will retry on failure, which is great for worker nodes with transient issues. Unfortunately failure to detect a face is a common user input error occuring in just around half of all image uploads. This will permanently tombstone these jobs.

The new failure class can be reused for future animation systems that rely on face detection.

There is still some minor work to do to surface this error to the frontend / user in a friendly way.

Migration

Functions

< 0.20 function 0.21 equivalent

encode_config() engine.encode()
encode_config_buf() engine.encode_string()
encode_config_slice() engine.encode_slice()

decode_config() engine.decode()
decode_config_buf() engine.decode_vec()
decode_config_slice() engine.decode_slice()

The short-lived 0.20 functions were the 0.13 functions with config replaced with engine.

Padding

If applicable, use the preset engines engine::STANDARD, engine::STANDARD_NO_PAD, engine::URL_SAFE, or engine::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD. The NO_PAD ones require that padding is absent when decoding, and the others require that canonical padding is present .

0.25.0

Breaking Changes

  • #261 Upgrade syn dependency to version 2. This bumps the msrv to 1.56. It's impractical to maintain a package where a core dependency of the ecosystem has a different msrv than this one.

  • 270 Change the to_string behavior when using default. Now, when using default, the display method will return the display version of the value contained in the enum rather than the name of the variant.

    #[derive(strum::Display)]
enum Color {
  Red,
  Blue,
  Green,
  #[strum(default)]
  Other(String)
}

    fn main() {
// This used to print "Other", now it prints "Purple"
assert_eq!(Color::Other("Purple".to_string()).to_string(), "Purple");
}

    If you want the old behavior, you can use the to_string attribute to override this behavior. See the PR for an example.

  • 268 Update the behavior of EnumCount to exclude variants that are disabled. This is a breaking change, but the behavior makes it more consistent with other methods.

  • #257 This PR adds the EnumIs macro that automatically implements is_{variant_name} methods for each variant.

title: tts-inference-job --> inference-job
author: echelon
body:
This makes it possible to run TT2 on inference-job. Once we roll this out to production, we can kill tts-inference-job. 

Features: 

- TT2 jobs can live on the `generic_inference_jobs` table instead of the specialized `tts_inference_jobs` table. 
- Job checking the old and the new endpoint work during the migration. The old endpoint is compatible with the new job tokens.
- TTS results endpoint is compatible with media_files. 

The inference job handles the following

- Health checking the TT2 sidecar and blocking until it reports healthy 
- Checking model dependency status and waiting until a job with a model on the filesystem arrives 

Remaining items left not completed

- Telling the TT2 sidecar which models to jettison from memory 
- Handling LFU cache ejection 
- Handling the difference between local filesystem cache and in-memory cache
- Cleaning up the filesystem when full 

(These can wait)

  • Full fix for the high-severity security vulnerability RUSTSEC-2024-0006 a.k.a. GHSA-r7qv-8r2h-pg27:
    • Deprecates quote APIs in favor of try_ equivalents that complain about nul bytes.
    • Also adds a builder API, which allows re-enabling nul bytes without using the deprecated interface, and in the future can allow other things (as discussed in quoting_warning).
    • Adds documentation about various security risks that remain, particularly with interactive shells.

1.2.1

  • Partial fix for the high-severity security vulnerability RUSTSEC-2024-0006 a.k.a. GHSA-r7qv-8r2h-pg27 without bumping MSRV:

title: Bump image from 0.24.7 to 0.25.1
author: dependabot
body:
Bumps [image](https://github.com/image-rs/image) from 0.24.7 to 0.25.1.
Changelog

Sourced from image's changelog.

Version 0.25.1

Bug fixes:

  • Fixed corrupt JPEG output when attempting to encode images containing an alpha channel.
  • Only accept ".ff" file extension for farbfeld images.
  • Correct farbfeld feature flag for ImageFormat::{reading_enabled, writing_enabled}.
  • Disable strict mode for JPEG decoder.
  • Add nasm feature to optionally enable faster AVIF encoding.

Version 0.25.0

Breaking changes:

  • Added BufRead + Seek bound on many decoders.
  • Use ExtendedColorType instead of ColorType when encoding.
  • Removed ImageOutputFormat, GenericImageView::bounds, and several other deprecated items.
  • Removed incremental decoding support and changed ImageDecoder so the trait is object safe.
  • Pixel types are now repr(transparent) rather than repr(C).
  • Made color_quant dependency optional.
  • Renamed some feature flags.

Structural changes:

  • Increased MSRV to 1.67.1

Codec changes:

  • Switched to image-webp for WebP encoding.
  • Switched to zune-jpeg for JPEG decoding.
  • Made the HDR decoder produce f32 images.
  • Removed DXT encoding and decoding support.

Version 0.24.9

impl<T: NoUninit> From<Box<T>> for BoxBytes

author: dependabot
body:
Bumps [quick-xml](https://github.com/tafia/quick-xml) from 0.30.0 to 0.32.0.
Release notes

Sourced from quick-xml's releases.

v0.32.0

Significant Changes

The method of reporting positions of errors has changed - use error_position() to get an offset of the error position. For SyntaxErrors the range error_position()..buffer_position() also will represent a span of error.

:warning: Breaking Changes

The way to configure parser has changed. Now all configuration is contained in the Config struct and can be applied at once. When serde-types feature is enabled, configuration is serializable.

The way of resolve entities with unescape_with has changed. Those methods no longer resolve predefined entities (lt, gt, apos, quot, amp). NoEntityResolver renamed to PredefinedEntityResolver.

Writer::create_element now accepts impl Into<Cow<str>> instead of &impl AsRef<str>.

Minimum supported version of serde raised to 1.0.139

The full changelog is below.

What's Changed

New Features

  • #513: Allow to continue parsing after getting new Error::IllFormed.
  • #677: Added methods config() and config_mut() to inspect and change the parser configuration. Previous builder methods on Reader / NsReader was replaced by direct access to fields of config using reader.config_mut().<...>.

title: Bump ring from 0.17.8 to 0.17.12
author: dependabot
body:
Bumps [ring](https://github.com/briansmith/ring) from 0.17.8 to 0.17.12.
Changelog

Sourced from ring's changelog.

Version 0.17.12 (2025-03-05)

Bug fix: briansmith/ring#2447 for denial of service (DoS).

  • Fixes a panic in ring::aead::quic::HeaderProtectionKey::new_mask() when integer overflow checking is enabled. In the QUIC protocol, an attacker can induce this panic by sending a specially-crafted packet. Even unintentionally it is likely to occur in 1 out of every 2**32 packets sent and/or received.

  • Fixes a panic on 64-bit targets in ring::aead::{AES_128_GCM, AES_256_GCM} when overflow checking is enabled, when encrypting/decrypting approximately 68,719,476,700 bytes (about 64 gigabytes) of data in a single chunk. Protocols like TLS and SSH are not affected by this because those protocols break large amounts of data into small chunks. Similarly, most applications will not attempt to encrypt/decrypt 64GB of data in one chunk.

Overflow checking is not enabled in release mode by default, but RUSTFLAGS="-C overflow-checks" or overflow-checks = true in the Cargo.toml profile can override this. Overflow checking is usually enabled by default in debug mode.

title: Bump pyo3 from 0.22.6 to 0.24.1
author: dependabot
body:
Bumps [pyo3](https://github.com/pyo3/pyo3) from 0.22.6 to 0.24.1.
Release notes

Sourced from pyo3's releases.

v0.24.1

This release is a security fix for the PyString::from_object method, which passed &str data to the Python C API without checking for a terminating nul byte. All historical PyO3 versions are affected, and we recommend you upgrade if you are using PyString::from_object. Thank you to @​vthib for the report and @​Dr-Emann for the fix. A RUSTSEC advisory will be published shortly.

Aside from the security fix, this release contains a number of other non-breaking additions:

  • An abi3-py313 feature to support compiling with the Python 3.13 stable ABI.
  • PyAnyMethods::getattr_opt to get optional attributes without paying the cost of a Python exception when the attribute in question does not exist.
  • Constructor for PyInt::new.
  • with_critical_section2 for locking two objects at the same time on the free-threaded build.
  • Fix for a PyO3 0.24.0 regression with Option<&str> and Option<&T> (where T: PyClass) function arguments no longer being permitted

There are also a few other small bug fixes for edge cases, mostly related to compile errors from PyO3's macro code.

Thank you to the following contributors for the improvements:

@​bschoenmaeckers @​davidhewitt @​Dr-Emann @​emmagordon

author: dependabot
body:
Bumps [esbuild](https://github.com/evanw/esbuild) to 0.25.2 and updates ancestor dependencies [esbuild](https://github.com/evanw/esbuild), [@vitejs/plugin-react](https://github.com/vitejs/vite-plugin-react/tree/HEAD/packages/plugin-react), [vite](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/tree/HEAD/packages/vite) and [vite-plugin-static-copy](https://github.com/sapphi-red/vite-plugin-static-copy). These dependencies need to be updated together. Updates `esbuild` from 0.21.5 to 0.25.2
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.25.2

  • Support flags in regular expressions for the API (#4121)

    The JavaScript plugin API for esbuild takes JavaScript regular expression objects for the filter option. Internally these are translated into Go regular expressions. However, this translation previously ignored the flags property of the regular expression. With this release, esbuild will now translate JavaScript regular expression flags into Go regular expression flags. Specifically the JavaScript regular expression /\.[jt]sx?$/i is turned into the Go regular expression `(?i)\.[jt]sx?$` internally inside of esbuild's API. This should make it possible to use JavaScript regular expressions with the i flag. Note that JavaScript and Go don't support all of the same regular expression features, so this mapping is only approximate.

  • Fix node-specific annotations for string literal export names (#4100)

    When node instantiates a CommonJS module, it scans the AST to look for names to expose via ESM named exports. This is a heuristic that looks for certain patterns such as exports.NAME = ... or module.exports = { ... }…

Tokio v1.44.2

This release fixes a soundness issue in the broadcast channel. The channel accepts values that are Send but !Sync. Previously, the channel called clone() on these values without synchronizing. This release fixes the channel by synchronizing calls to .clone() (Thanks Austin Bonander for finding and reporting the issue).

Fixed

  • sync: synchronize clone() call in broadcast channel (#7232)

#7232: tokio-rs/tokio#7232

Tokio v1.44.1

Fixed

  • rt: skip defer queue in block_in_place context (#7216)

#7216: tokio-rs/tokio#7216

Tokio v1.44.0

1.44.0 (March 7th, 2025)

This release changes the from_std method on sockets to panic if a blocking socket is provided. We determined this change is not a breaking change as Tokio is not intended to operate using blocking sockets. Doing so results in runtime hangs and should be considered a bug. Accidentally passing a blocking socket to Tokio is one of the most common user mistakes. If this change causes an issue for you, please comment on #7172.

title: Bump tracing-subscriber from 0.3.19 to 0.3.20
author: dependabot
body:
Bumps [tracing-subscriber](https://github.com/tokio-rs/tracing) from 0.3.19 to 0.3.20.
Release notes

Sourced from tracing-subscriber's releases.

tracing-subscriber 0.3.20

Security Fix: ANSI Escape Sequence Injection (CVE-TBD)

Impact

Previous versions of tracing-subscriber were vulnerable to ANSI escape sequence injection attacks. Untrusted user input containing ANSI escape sequences could be injected into terminal output when logged, potentially allowing attackers to:

  • Manipulate terminal title bars
  • Clear screens or modify terminal display
  • Potentially mislead users through terminal manipulation

In isolation, impact is minimal, however security issues have been found in terminal emulators that enabled an attacker to use ANSI escape sequences via logs to exploit vulnerabilities in the terminal emulator.

Solution

Version 0.3.20 fixes this vulnerability by escaping ANSI control characters in when writing events to destinations that may be printed to the terminal.

Affected Versions

All versions of tracing-subscriber prior to 0.3.20 are affected by this vulnerability.

Recommendations

Immediate Action Required: We recommend upgrading to tracing-subscriber 0.3.20 immediately, especially if your application:

  • Logs user-provided input (form data, HTTP headers, query parameters, etc.)
  • Runs in environments where terminal output is displayed to users

Migration

This is a patch release with no breaking API changes. Simply update your Cargo.toml:

[dependencies]
tracing-subscriber = "0.3.20"

Acknowledgments

We would like to thank zefr0x who responsibly reported the issue at security@t…

Change Log

All user visible changes to this project will be documented in this file. This project adheres to Semantic Versioning, as described for Rust libraries in [RFC #1105](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/blob/master/text/1105-api-evolution.md). We explicitly reserve the right to perform breaking changes in minor releases to fix build breaking changes from the Rust project. For any named minimal supported Rust version we guarantee that it is possible to build Diesel with the default features enabled using some set of dependencies. Those set of dependencies is not necessarily an up to date version of the specific dependency. We check this by using the unstable -Z minimal-version cargo flag. Increasing the minimal supported Rust version will always be coupled at least with a minor release.

Release notes

Sourced from pnpm's releases.

pnpm 10.27

Minor Changes

  • Adding trustPolicyIgnoreAfter allows you to ignore trust policy checks for packages published more than a specified time ago#10352.

  • Added project registry for global virtual store prune support.

    Projects using the store are now registered via symlinks in {storeDir}/v10/projects/. This enables pnpm store prune to track which packages are still in use by active projects and safely remove unused packages from the global virtual store.

  • Semi-breaking. Changed the location of unscoped packages in the virtual global store. They will now be stored under a directory named @ to maintain a uniform 4-level directory depth.

  • Added mark-and-sweep garbage collection for global virtual store.

    pnpm store prune now removes unused packages from the global virtual store's links/ directory. The algorithm:

    1. Scans all registered projects for symlinks pointing to the store
    2. Walks transitive dependencies to mark reachable packages
    3. Removes any package directories not marked as reachable

    This includes support for workspace monorepos - all node_modules directories within a project (including those in workspace packages) are scanned.

Patch Changes

v6.24.0

Undici v6.24.0 Security Release Notes (LTS)

This release backports fixes for security vulnerabilities affecting the v6 line.

Upgrade guidance

All users on v6 should upgrade to v6.24.0 or later.

Fixed advisories

  • GHSA-2mjp-6q6p-2qxm / CVE-2026-1525 (Medium)
    Inconsistent interpretation of HTTP requests (request/response smuggling class issue).

  • GHSA-f269-vfmq-vjvj / CVE-2026-1528 (High)
    Malicious WebSocket 64-bit frame length handling could crash the client.

  • GHSA-4992-7rv2-5pvq / CVE-2026-1527 (Medium)
    CRLF injection via the upgrade option.

title: Feature: Multifile upload
author: tanish2k09
body:
Notable behavior:

- Mixing supported and/or unsupported file types will only keep files of file type that match the first supported file type in the list received from browser (e.g. PNG, OBJ, EXE, JPG, OBJ order selection of files will only show PNG, JPG for image upload)
- Removing files until only one is left will result in the sidebar vanishing and only a single preview showing. More files can be added by selecting multiple files again through the file selection button
- Failure to upload has been handled but not tested. It is expected any failed uploads could be retried with a "retry failed" button. Any individual fail can also be retried via a retry button upon hovering on the exclamation mark by the failed file's name
- All multi-file uploads are queued async and likely wouldn't be ordered as shown in the preview list (first-come-first-serve)
- Potentially deadlocks if a task never responds. Likely handled by backend timeouts. This deadlock state is only partial and not lossy as successfully uploaded files will appear in gallery even if the task is cancelled. Cancellation can be attempted at any point during the upload. Uploads shown in progress may be successful after cancellation depending on the internal upload progress.
- TopBar upload images button now opens the image modal instead for consistency and same-component use.

title: Fix: Allow asset.localhost in CSP for Windows drag-drop
author: tanish2k09
body: On Windows production builds, convertFileSrc() generates https://asset.localhost/... URLs. The connect-src CSP only had "asset:" (covering asset:// on macOS/Linux) but not https://asset.localhost, causing the fetch() in GlobalFileDropHandler to be silently blocked — overlay appeared but no modal opened on drop.

title: Fix blank screen crash and text selection loss in video prompt box
author: frankywashere
body:
## Summary
- **Fix blank screen crash** during video recreate flow: typing text, adjusting time slider, typing again, then clicking the text box caused an uncaught DOM exception in MentionTextarea's contentEditable caret operations, which unmounted the entire React tree (no error boundaries existed)
- **Fix text selection disappearing** on mouse release in MentionTextarea: click handler and sync useEffect were destroying active selections by rewriting innerHTML and restoring only a collapsed caret
- **Add React Error Boundary** around PromptBoxVideo as a safety net

## Changes
### MentionTextarea.tsx
- Wrap `getCaretOffset`, `setCaretOffset`, `scrollCaretIntoView`, `handleInput`, sync `useEffect`, and `getOffsetRect` in try/catch to prevent uncaught DOMExceptions
- Add null guard for `childNodes` iteration and `parentNode` access
- Skip `detectMention` in `handleClick` when user has active text selection
- Skip innerHTML rewrite in sync useEffect when editor has selected text

### PromptBoxVideo.tsx
- Stabilize `characterNames` with `useMemo` to prevent `mentionColorMap` from rebuilding every render
- Move empty characters array to module-level constant for stable reference
- Add cleanup `useEffect` for `durationTimerRef` to prevent stale timer after unmount

### New: PromptBoxErrorBoundary.tsx
- React Error Boundary with "Try again" recovery button

### ImageToVideo.tsx
- Wrap `<PromptBoxVideo>` with `<PromptBoxErrorBoundary>`

## Reproduction steps (original bug)
1. Click "Recreate" on a video
2. Type text into the prompt box
3. Adjust the time slider
4. Type text again
5. Adjust the time slider and click the text box → **UI goes blank**

## Test plan
- [x] Reproduced blank screen bug on Mac before fix
- [x] Verified fix: repeated recreation flow no longer causes blank screen
- [x] Verified text selection persists after mouse release
- [x] Video generation with @mentions, reference images, and duration changes works correctly

Release notes

Sourced from axios's releases.

v1.15.0

This release delivers two critical security patches, adds runtime support for Deno and Bun, and includes significant CI hardening, documentation improvements, and routine dependency updates.

⚠️ Important Changes

  • Deprecation: url.parse() usage has been replaced to address Node.js deprecation warnings. If you are on a recent version of Node.js, this resolves console warnings you may have been seeing. (#10625)

🔒 Security Fixes

  • Proxy Handling: Fixed a no_proxy hostname normalisation bypass that could lead to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). (#10661)
  • Header Injection: Fixed an unrestricted cloud metadata exfiltration vulnerability via a header injection chain. (#10660)

🚀 New Features

title: Fix @mention tagging in prompts with CJK characters
author: bflatastic
body:
Two bugs were preventing @image / @video / @character references from
being tagged in prompts written with Chinese, Japanese, or Korean text:

1. The mention-highlight regex was built with just the "g" flag, so a
   user-typed "@image6" never matched the canonical label "@Image6" and
   the reference was rendered as plain text. Make the regex
   case-insensitive and do the colorMap lookup via a lowercase-keyed
   table so "@image6" still finds the color for "@Image6".

2. detectMention required the character immediately before "@" to match
   /\s/, which never matches CJK characters. Typing "@" right after a
   Chinese character like "从" therefore never opened the autocomplete
   dropdown, leaving users to type the mention by hand (which then hit
   bug 1). Replace the whitespace check with a "not an ASCII identifier
   char" check so CJK, quotes, and punctuation all count as valid word
   boundaries before an @mention.

Release notes

Sourced from axios's releases.

v1.16.0 — May 2, 2026

This release adds support for the QUERY HTTP method and a new ECONNREFUSED error constant, lands a substantial wave of HTTP, fetch, and XHR adapter bug fixes around redirects, aborts, headers, and timeouts, and welcomes 23 new contributors.

⚠️ Notable Changes

A handful of fixes in this release are either security-adjacent or change observable behaviour. Please review before upgrading:

  • Fetch adapter now enforces maxBodyLength and maxContentLength. These limits were silently ignored on the fetch adapter prior to 1.16.0 — anyone relying on them as a safety net (DoS protection, accidental large uploads) had no protection. (#10795)
  • Proxy requests now preserve user-supplied Host headers. Previously, the proxy path could overwrite a custom Host. Virtual-host-style routing through a proxy will now behave correctly. (#10822)
  • Basic auth credentials embedded in URLs are now URL-decoded. If you have percent-encoded credentials in a URL (e.g. https://user:p%40ss@host), the decoded value is what now goes on the wire. (#10825)
  • parseProtocol now strictly requires a colon in the protocol separator. Strings that loosely parsed as protocols before may no longer match. (#10729)

title: pagescene AssetMenu: fix featured Sets/Creatures never loading
author: tanish2k09
body:
## Summary

- Regression from PR #1492. After the refactor, `useFeaturedObjects` auto-fetch effect was racing the `EngineContext` editor instance: on AssetModal's first mount `editor` is `null`, the effect synchronously flipped `firstFetch.current` to `IN_PROGRESS` and then called `fetchFeaturedObjects()` which immediately bailed at `if (!editor) return`. When the editor became available the effect re-fired (editor is in the `useCallback` deps), but the `IN_PROGRESS` guard then blocked it — so **the network request never fired** for any featured category.
- Visible only on Sets and Creatures tabs because Characters/Objects/Memes are merged with local demo arrays in `assetTabs` and looked populated despite the same fetch breakage.
- Fix: gate the auto-fetch effect on `editor` (early-return when null, add `editor` to deps) so `IN_PROGRESS` isn't burned on the no-op call.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open `/edit-3d` in artcraft-webapp with DevTools Network panel + "Disable cache" on.
- [ ] Open the AssetModal — confirm exactly 5 GETs to `/v1/media_files/list_featured` (one each for `character`, `object`, `location`, `creature`, `image_plane`).
- [ ] Switch to Sets and Creatures tabs — items render.
- [ ] Drag a Set into the 3D scene — loads via `addObject` (LOCATION maps to `AssetType.OBJECT` in `responseMapping`).
- [ ] Tauri smoke: open the 3D page in the desktop app, AssetModal Sets/Creatures tabs populate.
- [ ] `nx typecheck @storyteller/ui-pagescene` (no new errors).

Adds a Blender/Photoshop-style **splash modal** to `/edit-3d` so anonymous visitors and first-time signed-in users land on a clear choice - *Blank scene* or one of a few example scenes - instead of an empty viewport with no orientation. Also reworks the demo output overlay (now hide-able + click-to-expand) and gives the **Controls3D toolbar** a floating, design-coherent treatment that matches the rest of the editor's UI language.

## Highlights

- **Edit-3D splash**: auto-opens for anon (every visit) and first-time logged-in users (gated by `localStorage["edit_3d_splash_seen_v1"]`). Skips when the URL already has a scene token. Always re-triggerable from **File > New Scene**.
- **Demo output overlay**: click the image to expand, X steps down a level (expanded → PIP → hidden), `Show output` pill brings it back. Restyled to the editor's `glass` / `bg-ui-controls` palette.
- **Controls3D toolbar**: floating `rounded-2xl glass` pill, tightened spacing, lower-opacity dividers, World/Local button gets an icon + matched palette + fixed width so it doesn't shift on toggle.
- New `hostOverlayVisible` flag in the lib's `PageSceneStore` lets the webapp host suppress in-editor affordances (e.g. the bouncing "Click + to add" hint) while a modal is up.

## New files

```
frontend/apps/artcraft-webapp/src/pages/pagescene/splash/
├── index.ts                       barrel
├── scene-splash-store.ts          Zustand isOpen/open/close
├── example-scenes.ts              placeholder example data (sceneToken + outputToken)
├── useSceneSplashAutoOpen.ts      auto-open effect + localStorage gating
├── useSceneSplashActions.ts       pickBlank / pickExample handlers
├── useSceneSplashLibSync.ts       mirrors isOpen → lib's hostOverlayVisible
├── SceneSplashCard.tsx            reusable card (blank + example variants)
└── SceneSplashModal.tsx           presentation shell
```

Each file is single-responsibility; `pagescene.tsx` integration is three lines.

title: Fix desktop video generation ignoring selected resolution
author: tanish2k09
body:
The desktop video promptbox built the GenerateVideoRequest without ever setting `resolution`, so generation always omitted it and the backend fell back to the model's default (720p) — and billed for it. The cost preview reads the same store value and sends it, so the preview was correct (e.g. 117 for 480p) while the charge stayed at the 720p price (240). Populate request.resolution in buildRequest, mapping the store's legacy display string ("480p"/"720p"/"1080p") to CommonResolution, guarded on the model exposing resolutionOptions.

Also fix useImageCostEstimate (webapp) omitting `quality` from its effect deps, which meant the image cost preview didn't refresh when only the quality option changed.

title: Fix login modal: stop Reveal motion wrappers from stealing input focus
author: tanish2k09
body:
Reveal/RevealGroup called `motion(as)` inside the render body. Unlike the cached `motion.div` accessor, calling `motion()` as a function returns a brand-new component type on every invocation. So each re-render produced a different element type at that position, React unmounted and remounted the whole subtree, and any focused <input> inside (the login/signup/forgot-password forms) lost focus on every keystroke — you could only type one character at a time.

Cache one motion component per element type via a module-level map so the component reference stays stable across renders. React now reconciles in place and focus is preserved.

Verified with a Playwright A/B test on the login form: before the fix typing "test@example.com" left only "t" with focus on <body> (1 blur mid-type); after the fix the full value is retained, focus stays on the input, zero blurs.

title: Keybind settings: New menu and revamped keybind support
author: tanish2k09
body:
## Summary

Adds a unified, remappable keyboard-shortcut system (`@storyteller/keybinds`) across the webapp and desktop app, replacing the scattered hardcoded `keydown` listeners in the 3D editor, 2D editor, and moodboard with one registry, two presets (**Gamer** = today's defaults, **Blender-like**), a Settings → Keybinds pane, and a hold-Ctrl / pinnable cheatsheet on every editor surface.

This PR was approved in June and then sat behind ~195 commits on `main` (timeline, build/record modes, lucide migration). It has been merged with current `main` and extended to cover the features that landed since. **Nothing changes by default** — the Gamer preset reproduces every existing key exactly.

## Architecture

- **Registry of `ActionDef`s** keyed by surface-namespaced ids (`pagescene.timeline.playPause`), bound to physical `event.code`. Resolution: user override → preset delta → base bindings. Persisted in the `artcraft-keybinds` zustand store.
- **Five surfaces**: `global`, `pagescene` (3D), `pagedraw` (2D), `moodboard` (canvas), `moodboard-grid` (board library / inspector / presentation).
- **Declared availability** — `ActionDef.when(ctx)` gates decide whether a binding is live for the current editor state (`sceneMode`, `encoding`, `timelineExpanded`, `timelineSelection`, …). An unavailable binding falls through *without consuming the event*, which is what lets Space / arrows / Delete / Escape be shared by context-exclusive actions. A sampled-context checker (`actionsCoAvailable`) proves the exclusivity in tests and drives the conflict UI in Settings.
- **Global surface is a pure trigger layer**: features register behavior with `useGlobalAction(id, handler)`; a window capture-phase dispatcher fires above the modal key-swallow, and an unregistered binding is inert per host. First inhabitant: Ctrl/Cmd+B sidebar. This is the intended home for the upcoming privacy-blur toggle (one `ActionDef` + one binding + one `useGlobalAction` call).
- Cross-surface conflict detection…

title: Webapp/website: Require signup before Stripe checkout
author: bflatastic
body:
Logged-out users clicking a purchase button used to be sent straight to Stripe,
relying on auto account creation after payment. They now create an account
first, then land in Stripe checkout for the plan they originally clicked.

**Flow:**
1. Logged-out user clicks "Get Plan" on any pricing table (webapp or website)
2. They are redirected to `/signup?plan=<slug>&cadence=<yearly|monthly>`
3. After signup (email or Google SSO), we call the normal logged-in
   subscription checkout API and redirect to Stripe for that exact plan
4. Existing users can switch to `/login` (params are preserved) and get the
   same checkout redirect after logging in
5. Logged-in users are unaffected: they still go straight to checkout / plan
   switch

**Changes:**
- `pricing-table`: logged-out plan clicks navigate to signup with the plan in
  the query string instead of calling the signup-checkout API
- New shared `checkout-intent` helper in `@storyteller/ui-pricing-table`:
  builds/parses the query params (validates plan slugs) and starts Stripe
  checkout
- Signup and login pages in both apps resume checkout when the params are
  present; auth page links carry the params across signup/login
- Removed the unused `BillingApi.UserSignupSubscriptionCheckout` frontend
  method (backend endpoint untouched, can be retired separately)

title: easyenv: add test coverage for typed env var getters
author: amitkojha05
body:
## Summary

easyenv had no test coverage for boolean, num, string, or duration getters, despite being used across every service and job in the workspace. adds 34 tests covering the optional/required/or_default triad for each type.tests use unique env var names per test instead of adding `serial_test` dev-dep — `env::set_var` is process-global so cargo's
default parallel execution can race. cleanup via a `Drop` guard (`EnvVarGuard`, in `tests_common.rs`) so a panicking test doesn't leak state into its neighbors.

## follow-up

left `pathbuf.rs` for a separate PR — it depends on `storyteller_root::get_substituted_path` which needs more setup than belongs in this diff.

## behaviors these tests pin down but don't change

- boolean parsing only accepts `true` / `TRUE` / `false` / `FALSE` — `"1"`, `"0"`, `"yes"`, `"no"` return `ParseError`
- duration parses whole seconds only, no `"5s"` style suffixes

worth flagging in case either is intentional and someone wants to loosen these separately.

## verification

- `cargo test --package easyenv --test-threads=8` — 34/34 pass, no flakes across 20 consecutive runs
- `cargo clippy --package easyenv -- -D warnings` — clean

title: easyenv: reject env var names with equals signs or NUL bytes
author: amitkojha05
body:
## Summary

fixes the two `// TODO: EnvError enum variant for equals sign in env var name` comments in `boolean.rs` and `pathbuf.rs`. before this, `get_env_bool_required("FOO=BAR")` returned `Err(EnvError::NotUnicode)` on POSIX — misleading since the value isn't the problem, the name is a programming error.

## changes

- added `EnvError::InvalidVariableName { name, reason }`
- added `InvalidNameReason` enum: `Empty` / `ContainsEquals` / `ContainsNul`
- `pub(crate) validate::validate_env_name()` runs at the top of every typed getter (public wrappers only; the internal `_internal` fns are now unreachable with invalid names, so the TODO comments there are removed)
- `EnvError::Display` for the new variant notes it's a programming error, not an env misconfiguration
- tests covering all three rejection reasons across all five type modules

## scope

the original TODOs were only in `boolean.rs` and `pathbuf.rs`, but the same bug class exists in `num`, `string`, `duration` — applied validation to all five for consistency.self-review caught two inverted assertions in the bool `or_default` tests (was `assert!(!default)`, should have been asserting the default value comes back). fixed and re-verified.

## verification

- `cargo test --package easyenv` — 34 previous + 40 new tests pass
- `cargo check --workspace` — clean, no downstream match arms break (existing consumers use `?` or `_ =>` fallbacks)

title: web_base64: fix data URL decode bug, add encoder, add tests
author: amitkojha05
body:
## Summary

fixes a correctness bug in `web_base64_decode`, adds the missing encoder, and adds a test suite.

## the decode bug

per RFC 2397, data URLs come in two forms:

    data:<mime>;base64,<base64_payload>      # base64
    data:<mime>,<percent_encoded_payload>    # NOT base64

before this, `web_base64_decode` stripped the `data:...` prefix and always base64-decoded whatever was after the comma — so `web_base64_decode("data:text/plain,Hello%20World")` either returned garbage or a confusing base64 error. now returns `Err(WebBase64Error::NotBase64Encoded)`.

## changes

- `WebBase64Error` enum (`NotBase64Encoded` / `MalformedDataUrl` / `DecodeError`) using `thiserror`
- rewrote the decoder to check for `;base64` in the metadata segment before decoding
- added `web_base64_encode(bytes, mime_type)` — the crate was decode-only, so every caller producing a data URL         was reinventing  it
- test suite covering round-trip with/without mime type, both data URL forms, malformed input, invalid base64, empty input, full-range binary data

## downstream

return type changed from `Result<Vec<u8>, base64::DecodeError>` to `Result<Vec<u8>, WebBase64Error>`.

one caller found (`save_base64_image_to_temp_dir.rs` / `ArtcraftError`), migrated via a `From<WebBase64Error> for
ArtcraftError` impl. the `DecodeError` arm reuses the existing `ArtcraftError::DecodeError(base64::DecodeError)` variant since the inner type matches exactly. non-decode errors fall through to `ArtcraftError::AnyhowError`.

## verification

- `cargo check -p web_base64` / `cargo test -p web_base64` — 10/10  pass
- `ArtcraftError::DecodeError` and `From<base64::DecodeError>`  confirmed via `git grep` to match the reused variant exactly

title: Fix: silent failures when submitting a generation (recreate "does nothing" bug)
author: bflatastic
body:
Users reported that after using **Recreate**, pressing the generate arrow did nothing at all (no error, no card, no spinner). Root cause: several failure paths gave zero feedback, so a rejected request looked like a dead button or an outage.

### Changes

- **Show real error messages.** The API layer now keeps the server's error message (e.g. "Image is required") instead of throwing it away, so users see why a generation was rejected.
- **Toast on every failed submit.** Image and video pages (webapp + website) now show an error toast when a generation fails to start. Previously, most failures were recorded invisibly and never shown.
- **Out of credits feedback on the website.** 402 responses now show a toast (webapp keeps its upgrade modal).
- **Network errors are announced** instead of failing silently.

author: bflatastic

**Batch download**
- Add multi-select mode to the create-video results feed (webapp + desktop) with a "Select" toggle in the topbar, checkboxes on completed items, and a floating download bar

title: Character mention chips + mention fixes
author: bflatastic
body:
### New stuff
- Character `@mentions` in the video promptbox now show as **chips with a thumbnail**, so you can see exactly which character is attached to the prompt
- Clicking a chip opens a menu to **Replace** (pick another character), **Preview** (view their image), or **Remove** the mention
- Chips behave like a single unit - one backspace deletes the whole mention, and removing/replacing can be undone with Ctrl+Z
- Copying prompt text still gives clean plain text (`@name ...`), and pasting it back restores the chips
- When two characters share a name, the one you actually picked is now the one that gets sent

### Fixes
- Mobile: the `@` autocomplete no longer goes off-screen - it stays inside the viewport, flips below the caret when needed, and taps select reliably
- Focus mode: the autocomplete no longer pushes the prompt sideways / causes overflow
- Enter-to-generate now works while the mention editor is active on the webapp

title: Webapp: mobile audio ref fixes
author: bflatastic
body:
- **Fixed: picking an audio reference on mobile opened the photo/video picker.** iPhones don't have an audio library, so the browser fell back to Photos - the only thing you could "attach as audio" was a video, and it silently uploaded as an audio ref. Audio pickers now open the Files app filtered to real audio files (MP3, WAV, M4A, FLAC…).
- **Non-audio files are now rejected with a clear error toast** instead of being silently attached (also covers drag & drop and Android's "any file" picker).
- **Fixed: limit warnings never appeared in the web app.** Errors like "Total audio duration cannot exceed 15s" from shared components were firing into a toast system the web app doesn't render. They're now routed to the app's own toasts, so length/limit errors actually show up.
- Applies to the create video, create audio, and desktop reference deck flows

title: Bug fix: mention textarea & reference deck

- **Reference add-menu no longer hides behind the sidebar** - it now renders above everything instead of getting clipped by the promptbox layers.
- **Character autocomplete is scrollable in focus mode** - the fullscreen prompt's scroll lock was blocking it; same fix for the chip menu's Replace list.

author: bflatastic

title: Refactor: replace fontawesome icons with lucide icons
author: bflatastic
body:
Removes Font Awesome entirely

### Changes

- All ~1,000 icon call sites now import Lucide components directly from `lucide-react` (`<PlayIcon className="..." />`); no FA packages, tokens, or `fa*` identifiers remain anywhere.
- New `@storyteller/icons` lib holds the pieces Lucide doesn't ship: `DynamicIcon` for runtime-chosen icons (`icon={loading ? LoaderCircleIcon : SaveIcon}`), 11 brand logos (Discord, TikTok, ...) as inlined CC BY 4.0 paths, and HD/SD quality badges drawn in Lucide's stroke style.
- Global `.lucide { display: inline-block; width/height: 1.2em }` rule in each app stylesheet: keeps icons font-relative like FA (1.2em compensates Lucide's 24px-viewBox/20px-grid padding) and undoes Tailwind preflight's `svg { display: block }`. Explicit `w-*`/`size-*` utilities still win.
- FA-only props migrated: `spin` → `animate-spin`, FA size strings → em values.
- Dropped `@fortawesome/*` + `@awesome.me` kit deps, both `.npmrc` files, and
  the FA rule in `shared-vite-config.ts` (now externalizes `lucide-react`).

title: Ignore stale asynchronous cost estimates
author: matthewpenkala
body:
## Summary

- Centralize asynchronous estimate request sequencing in a shared lifecycle helper.
- Make only the newest image, video, or splat estimate authoritative.
- Clear obsolete credits immediately when replacement work begins or a selection becomes ineligible.
- Reset loading and quote state on unmount, missing/unsupported models, endpoint failures, and non-success responses.
- Re-estimate when a same-ID model receives refreshed catalog capabilities.

## Why

An older network response could arrive after a newer selection and overwrite the current quote. Several early-return and error paths could also leave stale credits or loading state visible.

## Validation

- Focused lifecycle suite: 27/27 passed.
- Coverage includes out-of-order responses, selection removal, same-ID capability refresh, unmount, error, and inactive-page transitions.
- `git diff --check` and contribution-scope scans pass.

## Origin and scope

This change was isolated from a broader downstream integration and reduced to a generic, self-contained upstream contribution. Private deployment/release-specific material and artifacts are intentionally excluded.

title: Honor catalog video aspect-ratio defaults
author: matthewpenkala
body:
## Summary

- Hydrate a video model's catalog-declared default aspect ratio independently from option order.
- Preserve the current user choice while it remains supported.
- Resolve an invalid or missing choice to the declared default, then retain the first-option fallback for legacy catalogs.
- Use the same resolver for the control, generation request, and cost estimate.

## Why

The first advertised option is not necessarily the model's canonical default. Different consumers could therefore display, estimate, and submit different aspect ratios after model hydration or a model switch.

## Validation

- Focused resolver and listing-loader suite: 6/6 passed.
- Declared defaults, valid sticky choices, invalid future values, option-order preservation, and legacy fallback are covered.
- The new spec is formatter-clean; `git diff --check` and contribution-scope scans pass.

## Integration note

This PR and #1884 both touch `useVideoCostEstimate.ts`. The behaviors are complementary; if the estimate-lifecycle PR lands first, this branch will be rebased so the shared freshness guarantees remain intact.

## Origin and scope

This change was isolated from a broader downstream integration and reduced to a generic, self-contained upstream contribution. Private deployment/release-specific material and artifacts are intentionally excluded.

title: Fix desktop API host initialization ordering
author: matthewpenkala
body:
## Summary

- Install the native-configured Storyteller API host before mounting desktop REST consumers.
- Share concurrent host synchronization, cache only accepted hosts, and keep failures retryable.
- Render a fail-closed startup error when the native host is unavailable.
- Run a host-change session refresh after installation without making that refresh block the app shell.

## Why

Desktop startup previously launched host synchronization as fire-and-forget work from the rendered component tree. REST consumers could therefore mount against a default or stale host before Tauri configuration arrived.

The bootstrap now establishes the required host first while leaving web startup unchanged.

## Validation

- Focused host-sync and bootstrap suites: 16/16 passed.
- Concurrent callers, retry behavior, cache invalidation, missing-host failure, and noncritical session-refresh paths are covered.
- `git diff --check` and contribution-scope scans pass.

## Origin and scope

This change was isolated from a broader downstream integration and reduced to a generic, self-contained upstream contribution. Private deployment/release-specific material and artifacts are intentionally excluded.

title: Preserve explicit model choices during catalog hydration
author: matthewpenkala
body:
## Summary

- Track whether a model selection is automatic or explicitly chosen by the user.
- Let automatic selections follow the available default after catalog hydration.
- Preserve a still-valid explicit selection instead of silently replacing it.
- Rebind an explicit same-ID choice to the rebuilt catalog model so refreshed capabilities are not lost.

## Why

Catalog hydration rebuilds model instances and may change the available default. Without selection provenance, the reconciliation step could either overwrite a user's explicit choice or retain a stale model object with outdated capabilities.

## Validation

- Focused selector-store suite: 7/7 passed.
- Automatic fallback, explicit preservation, same-ID capability refresh, and page-scoped defaults are covered.
- `git diff --check` and contribution-scope scans pass.

## Origin and scope

This change was isolated from a broader downstream integration and reduced to a generic, self-contained upstream contribution. Private deployment/release-specific material and artifacts are intentionally excluded.

title: Preserve canonical video resolution during desktop Recreate
author: matthewpenkala
body:
## Summary

- Preserve exact API resolution values when the target video model advertises canonical options.
- Translate only `four_eighty_p`, `seven_twenty_p`, and `ten_eighty_p` for legacy label-based overlays.
- Reject missing, unsupported, and future values instead of guessing.

## Why

Recreate previously conflated canonical K-based values with presentation labels, including treating `one_k` as `1080p`. That can silently alter the next generation instead of restoring the recorded resolution.

## Validation

- Focused resolver suite: 13/13 passed.
- Canonical values, legacy labels, K-versus-1080p distinctions, missing data, and unknown future values are covered.
- `git diff --check` and contribution-scope scans pass.

## Origin and scope

This change was isolated from a broader downstream integration and reduced to a generic, self-contained upstream contribution. Private deployment/release-specific material and artifacts are intentionally excluded.

title: Honor video duration ranges and sparse duration options
author: matthewpenkala
body:
## Summary

- Hydrate continuous duration ranges, sparse duration options, defaults, and image-specific maximums from model listings.
- Resolve one effective duration contract for controls, generation requests, and cost estimates.
- Keep sparse choices index-driven so options such as `[5, 10]` cannot emit unsupported intermediate values.
- Apply image-duration caps only to media actually included in the effective request mode.
- Commit and send the value visible when Generate is pressed, including an immediately changed slider value.
- Clear stale estimates and keep estimate/request duration projection aligned.

## Why

Video listings can describe either continuous ranges or discrete supported durations. The existing prompt flow treated those contracts inconsistently, which could expose unsupported selections, estimate one duration while sending another, or apply an image cap to hidden media omitted from the request.

This centralizes the behavior without model-specific branching.

## Validation

Focused coverage exercises:

- valid and contradictory duration ranges;
- normalized, deduplicated sparse options;
- default and nearest-option selection;
- image-specific caps versus video/audio-only references;
- effective reference mode with stale hidden end-frame state;
- immediate selection followed by Generate;
- request/estimate projection parity; and
- stale estimate/loading cleanup.

`git diff --check` and contribution-scope scans pass.

## Integration status

This is the first layer of a deliberately serialized reference-media series. It also composes with the estimate-lifecycle work in #1884 and the aspect-default work in #1885. The PR is opened as a draft so those smaller shared-consumer changes can land first; this branch will then be rebased onto current `main`, revalidated, and marked ready without replacing either behavior.

title: Guard desktop version synchronization
author: matthewpenkala
body:
## What changed

- Added a desktop unit test that reads both Tauri bundle configurations.
- Fails when either configured bundle version differs from `ARTCRAFT_VERSION`.

## Why

The desktop runtime version and the macOS bundle version are maintained in separate files. A partial version bump can therefore produce a bundle whose metadata disagrees with the version reported by the running application.

## Impact

Release/version bumps now fail during the existing Rust test suite if the runtime, general Tauri configuration, and macOS Tauri configuration are not synchronized. Runtime behavior is unchanged.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p artcraft version -- --nocapture` (4 passed, including the new guard)
- `rustfmt --check crates/desktop/artcraft/src/version.rs`
- `git diff --check`
- CodeRabbit CLI review: 0 findings
- Gitleaks commit-range scan: no findings

title: Fix settings modal declaration build
author: matthewpenkala
body:
## What changed

- Builds the provider-priority list from the three providers supported by the desktop provider-order command.
- Ignores frontend-only provider enum variants and duplicate backend entries instead of indexing an incomplete map unsafely.
- Removes an unused credential-row local that also blocked declaration generation.
- Adds focused ordering and unsupported-provider tests.

## Why

The shared frontend `Provider` enum contains Grok and Midjourney, while the desktop provider-order command accepts only ArtCraft, Fal, and Sora. Treating the UI map as a complete `Record<Provider, ...>` caused a TypeScript declaration error; blindly adding the extra providers would send values the Rust command rejects.

## Impact

The settings-modal declaration build succeeds, supported provider ordering remains stable, omitted supported providers are appended, and unsupported variants are excluded from persisted desktop ordering.

## Validation

- Focused Vitest suite: 2 passed
- `nx run @storyteller/ui-settings-modal:build --skip-nx-cache` (library plus 40 dependencies passed)
- `nx run artcraft:build --skip-nx-cache` (application plus 58 dependencies passed)
- `git diff --check`
- Gitleaks commit-range scan: no findings

CodeRabbit CLI could not review this fourth branch because the free CLI allowance was exhausted after three successful reviews; the diff was reviewed manually and validated by the targeted and full desktop frontend builds above.

title: Test multiline prompt paste and focus-mode sizing
author: matthewpenkala
body:
## What changed

- add focused regression coverage for multiline prompt paste after edit/clear cycles
- verify replacement of an atomic mention preserves blank lines
- lock in the `min-h-0` fullscreen wrapper required for wheel scrolling

## Why

The underlying paste and focus-mode sizing fixes are already on `main`, but their state-dependent failure modes did not have direct component-level regression coverage. These tests protect the literal newline transaction and the flex shrink constraint without changing production behavior.

## Validation

- `npx nx run @storyteller/ui-promptbox:test --skip-nx-cache` — 3/3 tests passed; all 30 dependencies built
- targeted Prettier check passed
- targeted ESLint returned zero errors (the spec path is ignored by the current lint configuration)
- `git diff --check` passed

title: Keep SQLx codegen credentials out of process arguments
author: matthewpenkala
body:
## What changed

- disable shell tracing in the SQLx cache-regeneration helper
- pass the MySQL URL through the child environment instead of `--database-url`
- use unique temporary SQLite/staging paths with an exit cleanup trap
- fail clearly when no MySQL URL is configured

## Why

The previous helper could expose a credential-bearing MySQL URL through shell trace output and the `cargo sqlx` process arguments. The revised flow keeps that value out of logs and argv while preserving SQLite and MySQL cache generation semantics.

## Validation

- `bash -n script/rust/sqlx_codegen_database.sh` passed
- missing-credential path exited 1 with the intended diagnostic and no stdout
- MySQL prepare invocation was inspected to confirm the URL is supplied only via `DATABASE_URL`
- `git diff --check` passed

A live MySQL cache regeneration was not run because it requires a configured development database; the change does not modify query metadata or application runtime code.

title: Fix inflated cost quote after Recreate: measure restored ref durations
author: bflatastic
body:
Recreate restored reference videos/audios from the prompt record with duration: 0. The cost quote forwards that as a zero input-duration hint,and the backend deliberately prices a zero/unknown input at the worst-case 30-second billing maximum (Seedance 2.5 bills reference-video input seconds), so a recreated generation quoted far above the original charge — e.g. a 1080p 10s output with ~5s of input quotes 548 credits, but 1096 with the failsafe.

Measure each restored reference's duration from its CDN copy while
building the recreate payload, the same way the library "Send to prompt" path probes durations. Unmeasurable files keep 0 (worst-case quote as before; generation always bills from its own server-side measurement).

title: Fix "Checkout Cancelled" showing after successful plan switches via the stripe billing portal
author: bflatastic
body:
Users who switched plans (e.g. Pro to Max) were shown the "Checkout Cancelled - no payment
was made" page even though their upgrade went through and they were charged. Reported by
multiple users on Discord.

- Root cause: plan switches for existing subscribers go through the Stripe billing portal,
  which has a single return URL (`/portal_closed`) with no success/cancel distinction. Both
  apps redirected that URL to the Checkout Cancelled page, so successful upgrades looked
  like failed payments.
- Added a new `/checkout/portal-return` page to the webapp that checks the account's actual
  subscription state instead of assuming a cancellation:
  - Active plan found: shows a "You're on the {plan} plan" confirmation, with a note that
    credit adjustments from a plan switch can take a few minutes to appear.
  - No active plan: shows a neutral "Billing Session Closed" screen.
- Webapp: `/portal_closed` now routes to the new page instead of `/checkout/cancel`.
- Website: `/portal_closed` (the URL Stripe actually returns to) now redirects to the
  webapp's `/checkout/portal-return`; the legacy non-webapp fallback goes to `/pricing`
  instead of the cancel page.
- Added a breadcrumb entry for the new route.
- The real Checkout Cancelled page is unchanged and still handles genuine Stripe Checkout
  cancellations.

title: Fix page freeze after fast-closing the lightbox modal
author: bflatastic
body:
Opening a generated image/video and quickly clicking the backdrop to close left the whole page unclickable, with no visible overlay to explain why.

**Cause:** `Dialog.Overlay`/`Dialog.Content` are `forceMount`ed so react-spring owns the leave animation. On close `Dialog.Root`'s `open` flips false while the layer is still mounted, and Radix derives `disableOutsidePointerEvents` from that flag, so its cleanup never restores the `pointer-events: none` it set on `<body>`. Closing slowly masked it; closing fast interrupts the leave spring so the clearing render never comes.

**Fix:** `unregisterModal` now schedules `releaseStrandedBodyLock`, clearing a lock nothing still owns. Bails if a modal is still registered or a real open Radix dialog exists.

title: Upload OBJ, STL and PLY meshes by converting them to GLB
author: HEOJUNFO
body:
Closes #1210. FBX was already handled by the client-side FBX→GLB conversion. This adds OBJ, STL and PLY to the same path.

### Approach

`convertFbxToGlb.ts` says the pipeline after the picker (preview, backend asset, scene loader, timeline, Viewer3D) is glTF-only, so new formats are converted to GLB once rather than added as loaders everywhere. This PR keeps to that. OBJ/STL/PLY files enter the modal as `converting`, are parsed and exported in the existing Web Worker, and only the GLB is previewed and uploaded. No backend changes.

- **`modelToGlb.ts` (new):** one `convertModelBufferToGlb(buffer, ext, name)` used by both the worker and the main-thread fallback. These were two copies of the FBX parse + export.
  - **OBJ:** `OBJLoader` returns Phong materials, which glTF can't represent, so they are swapped for `MeshStandardMaterial` with the same color, map, vertex colors, side and opacity.
  - **STL / PLY:** the geometry is wrapped in a mesh. Vertex colors are kept (e.g. binary STLs with per-face color), and normals are computed when the file has none.
  - **PLY:** `.ply` is also the usual Gaussian-splat format. The header is read first: splat PLYs (`f_dc_0` / `scale_0` / `rot_0`) are rejected with a message pointing at `.spz`, and files with no `element face` (point clouds) are rejected too. This is checked on the header because `PLYLoader` de-indexes meshes that have per-face colors/UVs, so the parsed geometry can't tell a mesh from a point cloud.
- **`convertFbxToGlb` → `convertModelToGlb`:** same worker plumbing. The message now carries `ext` and `name`, and the worker returns `error.message` instead of `"Error: …"`.
- **`UploadFiles3D.tsx`:** the `isFbx` checks become `isConvertibleModelFile`, so the existing guarantees (no preview until converted, failed conversions retry the conversion, raw files never reach the backend) cover every format. Copy reads "Converting STL to GLB…" etc.
- **`GlobalFileDropHandler.tsx`:** window drag-and-drop only recognised `.glb`…

title: Free GPU resources on New Scene, object delete and skybox change
author: HEOJUNFO
body:
Three paths in the 3D stage remove objects without releasing the GPU memory they hold. Most visible on long sessions: every New Scene keeps the whole previous scene's textures and buffers alive.

### Cause

- **`Scene.clear()`** (called by `Editor.newScene()`): `this.scene.children = []` disposes nothing. It also skips `Object3D.remove`, so each child keeps `parent` pointing at the scene. All geometries, materials, textures and splat buffers of the previous scene stay on the GPU.
- **`SceneUtils.deleteObject()`**: disposes geometries and materials but not the textures they reference. `Material.dispose()` doesn't free `map`, `normalMap` etc., so deleting a textured GLB leaks every map. It also checks a custom `.texture` field that nothing in the codebase sets.
- **`Scene._create_skybox()`**: replaces `scene.background` with a new `CubeTexture` without disposing the old one. This happens on every skybox change and on New Scene.

### Fix

- **New `engine/disposeObject3D.ts`:** frees geometries, materials, the textures those materials reference (each shared material is disposed once), `SkinnedMesh` skeleton bone textures, and Spark `SplatMesh` buffers. Called after the tree is removed.
  - Geometry/material/texture disposal is safe even when shared with an object that stays, because three.js re-uploads on the next render.
  - `SplatMesh.dispose()` is not reversible. Each splat owns its own `PackedSplats` (one per `load_splat_wrapped_no_cors`), and `DeleteAction.revert()` re-loads from the snapshot instead of reusing the instance.
- **`clear()`:** `disposeObject3D(this.scene)` and then `this.scene.clear()`, so children are actually unparented.
- **`deleteObject()`:** the two hand-written traversal blocks are replaced by `disposeObject3D(obj)`.
- **`_create_skybox()`:** disposes the previous background texture first. Every branch replaces it.

### Testing

- `npx vitest run` in `libs/components/pagescene`: 6 new tests in `disposeObject3D.spec.ts` (nested textures, multi-m…

title: Linux: fix window sizing and NVIDIA crash, add build docs and publish workflow
author: echo3x3e
body:
Refs #1392

ArtCraft builds and runs on Linux from source with no changes to dependencies. This PR fixes three runtime problems I hit on a Linux desktop, documents the production build, and adds a Linux publish workflow.

## Changes

**1. Window opens larger than the screen and grows on every launch** (`initially_size_and_position_windows.rs`)

On Wayland with fractional scaling, GTK reports an integer scale factor, so the persisted physical size does not round-trip. The saved size grew on every launch (`5160x3056` → `5340x3332` on a 2560x1600 display), and the window controls ended up off-screen. Linux now skips restoring the persisted size and lets the window manager size the window. The restore logic moved unchanged into `restore_window_size()` for macOS and Windows.

**2. Default window size exceeds the screen** (`setup_main_window.rs`)

The default inner size of `2400x1300` is bigger than a 2560x1600 display at 125% scaling, which is 2048x1280 logical. KWin does not clamp it. Linux now starts the main window maximized.

**3. WebKitGTK crash on NVIDIA under Wayland** (`lib.rs`)

When the webview runs on the NVIDIA GPU, startup fails with:

```
Gdk-Message: Error 71 (Protocol error) dispatching to Wayland display.
ERROR: WebKit encountered an internal error. This is a WebKit bug.
```

The app now sets `__NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC=1` at the very start of `run()`, before any threads or GTK start, and only on Linux. A value the user has already set takes precedence, and other drivers ignore the variable.

**4. Docs** (`_docs/dev_setup.md`)

Adds a "Linux Production Build" section with the Arch package list, the `cargo tauri build --no-bundle` command, and the GPU notes.

## Observation, not changed in this PR

`WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1`, which `unix-dev.mjs` sets by default, made the **release** window transparent on KDE Wayland with an AMD iGPU: only `<video>` elements rendered. Without it, the release binary renders correctly on both the AMD and NVIDIA GPUs…

title: fix(upload-modal): keep uploaded images visible in the library
author: RafaelJaime
body:
## Problem

In the desktop app (macOS), uploading an image from the 3D Stage via **+ → Upload Image**:

1. The modal reports "Added Image to your library".
2. The library opens, but **All Assets**, **Image** and **Uploaded** all show "No items yet", even after refresh and with "Show uploads" ticked.
3. Since the image never appears, it can't be dragged into the scene.

Uploading the same file as a reference image on the **Create Image** page works, and it then shows up in the library.

## Cause

`uploadImage` in `libs/components/upload-modal` calls `MediaUploadApi.UploadImage` without `is_intermediate_system_file`. That parameter defaults to `EIntermediateFile.true` (`libs/api/src/lib/MediaUploadApi.ts`), which is correct for scene cover screenshots and masks but marks a user's upload as a hidden system file.

The prompt-box reference upload goes through `UploadImageMedia`, which passes `EIntermediateFile.false`, so it is listed.

The same modal backs the top-bar upload button and the global file drop handler, so those paths were affected too.

## Fix

Pass `is_intermediate_system_file: EIntermediateFile.false` from `uploadImage`. The shared default in `MediaUploadApi.UploadImage` is left as is, because cover images and masks rely on it.

## Tests

Added `uploadImage.spec.ts` (vitest, same setup as `loadPreviewOnCanvas.spec.ts`). It mocks `MediaUploadApi` and asserts that the upload is sent with `EIntermediateFile.false`, and that success reports the returned media token.

I have not run the suite locally, and I could not check the server side, which lives in `artcraft-services`. The diagnosis rests on the client code and on the working reference-upload path.

## Possibly related

Other `UploadImage` callers also rely on the default: Angles, ImageTo3D* and `upload-by-kind.ts`. I left them alone because I don't know whether those uploads are meant to stay hidden.

title: Fix WebKitGTK rendering on NVIDIA Linux and focus the login form
author: mattisking
body:
## Problem

On Linux with the NVIDIA proprietary driver and a Wayland compositor implementing `linux-drm-syncobj-v1` (e.g. KDE Plasma / KWin), the desktop app is unusable in several ways depending on the WebKitGTK configuration. All results below are from a single machine, verified repeatedly ([WebKit bug 280210](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=280210) is the upstream crash):

| Env configuration                     | Result on NVIDIA + KWin                                        |
|---------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| No flags (Wayland, DMABUF renderer on)| Crash at launch: GDK protocol error 71 (explicit sync used, but no acquire point is set) |
| WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1      | Transparent webview; only <video> elements render              |
| + WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE=1 (current launcher defaults) | Runs, but <video> paints above all DOM; login screen unusable |
| GDK_BACKEND=x11 (+ either of the above) | Black webview, or black with damage-only repaints           |
| __NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC=1          | **Everything renders correctly at full acceleration, video included** |

Environment: Fedora 44, webkit2gtk4.1 2.54.1, NVIDIA RTX 2060 SUPER with proprietary driver 615.71.09, KWin.

## Root cause

WebKitGTK 2.44+ commits DMABUF buffers through the explicit-sync timeline without ever calling `wp_linux_drm_syncobj_surface_v1.set_acquire_point`, so strict compositors terminate the connection (the upstream crash). The previous launcher workaround (`WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER` / `WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE`) avoided the crash but fell into WebKitGTK's broken fallback rendering paths, which is what the forced defaults were shipping to every Linux user of the dev launcher: with compositing disabled, HTML5 `<video>` elements paint above all other DOM, so the login screen was unusable on Linux regardless of GPU vendor.

- **New Linux-only startup module** (…

title: Disable NVIDIA explicit sync for WebKitGTK on Linux
author: BluePhi09
body:
Fixes #2055

Release builds crash on Wayland with NVIDIA's proprietary driver: `Error 71 (Protocol error)` / `networkProcessCrashed`, caused by the explicit-sync failure `Buffer attached but no acquire point set` ([WebKit bug 280210](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=280210)).

On Linux, `main()` now sets `__NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC=1` before any webview is created. It does this only when the NVIDIA kernel module is loaded (`/sys/module/nvidia`) and the variable isn't set already. Other drivers ignore the variable, and users can opt out with `__NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC=0`.

The first version of this PR set `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1` instead. That avoided the crash on sway, but on KWin the web view was fully transparent, both on NVIDIA ([test](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft/pull/2056#issuecomment-6115737953)) and on an AMD iGPU (#1993). `__NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC=1` renders on sway and on KWin and keeps GPU rendering (tested in #2031 and #1993). The Rust part of #2031 does the same thing; this PR is the minimal version without the frontend changes.

Known caveat: one report on WebKit bug 280210 (RTX 4090) saw flicker with this variable.

Not tested: I haven't compiled or run this revision myself.

title: Keep window controls reachable on the desktop login screen
author: JeremyYao
body:
## Problem

On first launch, the sign in / sign up screen blocks the minimize, maximize, and close buttons in the top right. On Windows the main window is created with `decorations(false)`, so the custom buttons in the TopBar are the only window controls there are. The login overlay is a full-screen layer at `z-[100]` while the TopBar sits at `z-[60]`, so the overlay covers both the buttons and the drag region. The window cannot be moved or closed until sign-in completes.

## Fix

- Extract the TopBar's three window buttons into a `WindowControls` component (`apps/artcraft/.../TopBar/WindowControls.tsx`). Same classes and behavior as before; it still renders nothing on macOS or in a plain browser. Aria-labels were added.
- `LoginModal` gains an optional `windowControls` slot. When provided, it renders a 56px `data-tauri-drag-region` strip pinned above the overlay backdrop with the controls flush right. The geometry matches the TopBar, so the icons land in the same spot and the window stays draggable.
- `MainApp` passes `<WindowControls />` into the modal.

Keeping the control cluster in the app and injecting it as a slot avoids giving the login-modal lib a dependency on the TopBar.

## Testing

- `login-modal` vitest suite passes (21 tests), including a new regression test that asserts the slot renders while the sign-up screen is showing.
- Touched files type-check cleanly against the workspace lib sources.
- Click-tested on a real Windows build; a manual check of minimize / maximize / close and drag on the login screen is working on my machine. 

## Out of scope

The generic `Modal` lib also covers the TopBar at `z-[70]`, so settings and pricing dialogs block the same buttons today. Those are dismissable, so they are left alone here, but the same slot pattern would fix them.

author: JeremyYao

## Summary

`.\script\artcraft\windows_rust_dev.ps1` failed to build on a machine with Visual Studio 2026 and Strawberry Perl. The desktop crate compiles BoringSSL from source through `wreq -> boring2 -> boring-sys2`, and that native build needs two things the setup docs do not mention:

- a CMake that knows the generator for the installed Visual Studio release. Strawberry Perl puts CMake 3.29 first on PATH, which does not know `Visual Studio 18 2026`, so CMake configuration failed with `Could not create named generator`.
- LLVM's libclang for bindgen, which was not installed.

These are the same prerequisites the Windows publish workflow installs with Chocolatey.

## Changes

- The script now gathers CMake candidates from PATH, Program Files, and the Visual Studio-bundled CMake (via vswhere), uses the newest one, and hands it to the Rust `cmake` crate through the `CMAKE` env var. A `CMAKE` value already set by the user is respected, and nothing is set when the newest CMake is already the one on PATH.
- A pre-flight check for `libclang.dll` prints an install hint if it is missing.

title: Reduce polling overhead and log noise
author: 0X11Dynamic
body:
Four small, independent changes found while profiling the desktop app's polling paths. No behavior changes beyond logging.

- **`fal_client`: reuse one HTTP client for queue polling.** `poll_job_status` and `poll_job_response` each called `reqwest::Client::new()` per request, so every poll (every 1-2s per pending FAL job) opened a new connection. They now share a `LazyLock<Client>`.
- **Third-party polling thread: log skipped non-FAL tasks at `debug`.** While another provider (Sora, Grok, Midjourney, World Labs) has a pending task, this loop logged one `warn!` per task every 2 seconds.
- **`TaskQueue.tsx`: remove the `console.log` of the full task queue result**, which ran on every 5s poll.
- **`signals/activeJobs.ts`: fix the dedupe in `setJobs`.** It called `deepEqual(setJobs, newJobList)`, comparing the function to the list, so it never matched and the signal was reassigned on every poll. It now compares `recentJobs.value`.

## Testing

- `SQLX_OFFLINE=true cargo check -p artcraft` passes.
- `cargo test -p fal_client --lib polling`: 21 passed, 4 ignored.
- `npx vite build` in `frontend/apps/artcraft` succeeds.
- Not run: the app itself. I did not measure the connection-reuse gain; it is a reasoning-based change.

title: Add artcraft-native: pure Rust (egui) desktop app, starting with Create Image and Create Video
author: bflatastic
body:
## What

A new workspace member, `artcraft-native/`. It is the ArtCraft desktop app in pure Rust: an egui UI with no Tauri, no webview and no JavaScript. It covers the two main product pages, **Create Image** and **Create Video**, and reuses the Tauri-free API crates (`artcraft_client`, `artcraft_api_defs`, `tokens`, `enums`).

It also adds:
- a Home page and a Library page
- a lightbox
- sign-in and settings dialogs
- a sidebar and top bar in the style of the brutalist **artcraft-webapp**

Tools that aren't ported yet show a "coming soon" page that links to the web app.

```bash
cargo run -p artcraft_native --release
```

## Why

To get a native, webview-free desktop app. Generation goes through **OmniGen** (`/v1/omni_gen/{models,cost,generate}`), the same API as the webapp. Model capabilities come from the server, so the pickers stay current without app updates.

## Prompt box

Recreated feature for feature from `PromptBoxImage` / `PromptBoxVideo`:
- **Editor:** auto-grow, focus mode, resize grip, length counter with the model's limit, Enter-to-generate setting, and `@Image1` / `@Video1` / `@Audio1` mentions with highlighting and autocomplete.
- **References:** the fanned reference deck (hover-expand, reorder, add menus with limits) and the first/last keyframe slots with swap. Files can be uploaded, picked from the library, dragged and dropped, or pasted as images.
- **Model selector:** families with a flyout, maker logos and capability badges.
- **Pickers:** aspect ratio, resolution, quality, count, bitrate, output format, duration slider, sound and input mode (Keyframe / Omni Reference).
- **Generate:** a live credit cost estimate, validation (starting frame, text-only models, limits, uploads in progress), and clear-all with confirmation.

The feed shows running jobs (with progress and time left), failures (dismissable), finished results and the paginated library, in a masonry grid or a list. It supports Recreate, Make Video, Share and Download, plus select mode…

title: artcraft-native: custom title bar and Claude-style layout
author: bflatastic

title: fix(timeline): prevent custom easing curves from snapping to endpoints
author: rudycelekli
body:
## Problem

The Motion popover permits both X handles at either edge of the curve. `cubicBezierYForX` uses unconstrained Newton iterations and clamps the final estimate. On valid flat-start and flat-end curves this can return an endpoint instead of the requested intermediate pose. For example, X(t)=t³ and Y(t)=t returns 1 at x=0.001 instead of 0.1; the actual `sampleTrackAt` path therefore jumps an animated object to its final transform.

## Change

Keep a bracket around the solution. Use Newton when its estimate stays within that bracket, and bisect otherwise, with a bounded 32-iteration limit. Preserve endpoint clamping and the existing easing data format.

## Verification

- Exact production module under the lockfile's Vitest 3.2.6: unchanged new tests reproduce **13 failures and 9 passing controls** before the fix, then **22 pass** afterward.
- Analytical t³ and mirrored flat-end controls cover slow derivatives; existing linear/endpoints and actual transform sampling are covered.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- This is module-level animation proof. I have not run a full signed Tauri build or live WebGL capture. A scoped TypeScript attempt follows the existing transform types into the wider app and is blocked by unavailable workspace dependencies; it is not claimed as passing.

AI assistance was used for investigation and tests. The patch and reproduction were independently reviewed.

title: fix(video-editor): accept leading decimals in property calculations
author: rudycelekli
body:
## Problem

Numeric property fields accept `.5` directly, but the arithmetic tokenizer rejects leading-decimal operands in expressions such as `.5 * 100` and `2 + .25`. Both existing property-draft hooks revert to the previous value instead of committing the calculation.

## Change

Allow the existing number scanner to start at a decimal point. Keep its existing finite-number validation and rejection of standalone/repeated decimal points; do not change expression precedence or introduce evaluation with `eval`.

## Verification

- Before: four parser regressions and two mounted real React hook regressions fail; twelve parser controls pass.
- After: all eighteen tests pass on this independent branch with lockfile-matching Vitest 3.2.6, React 18.3.1 and jsdom 22.1.0. Root independently replayed the eighteen tests in a separate worktree.
- Production-module strict TypeScript and `git diff --check` pass.
