AI assistance was used; the change was reproduced and independently reviewed.

title: fix(media): preserve queries and fragments when enabling CORS
author: rudycelekli
body:
## What changed

Enable CDN CORS without corrupting a media URL's existing query or fragment. The shared helper now appends `&cors=1` when a query exists, adds the flag before `#`, and normalizes an existing raw `cors` query parameter. It preserves the path and all other query bytes, including signed values.

## Why

Waveform audio and lightbox image/reference callers use this helper. The prior `${url}?cors=1` puts the flag inside an existing parameter value or inside a fragment, so the CDN never receives the flag. Native URL parsing and the real thumbnail helper paths reproduce this deterministically. This does not claim to reproduce the intermittent gallery navigation report in#1485.

## Tests

- Original upstream production source with frozen tests:10failed,1control passed.
- Final source:11native Vitest3.2.6/jsdom22.1tests passed.
- Controls cover existing signed query values, existing cors flags, relative URLs, fragment handling, actual thumbnail caller helpers, empty inputs and literal `&cors=` in paths.
- TypeScript5.8.3 strict production-module no-emit check and `git diff --check` passed.
- Full Nx/Tauri release build and live CDN/account flows were not run. Focused tests used an evidence-only config matching the library's jsdom/globals conventions.

AI-assisted investigation and implementation; reviewed with native regression evidence.

title: fix(promptbox): keep IME confirmation out of prompt actions
author: rudycelekli
body:
## What changed

Ignore prompt action keys while IME composition is active, including native `isComposing` and the 229 confirmation-key fallback. The guard precedes mention dropdown selection, newline insertion and the host key callback.

## Why

Input serialization already waits for composition, but keyboard actions did not. Confirming an IME candidate with Enter could insert a newline or call the host's Enter-to-generate handler; Enter/Tab could also replace the composing text with a mention. Normal keyboard behavior resumes after composition ends.

## Tests

Native mounted React component: six reproduced failures and two ordinary-Enter controls before the fix; all eight tests pass afterward. Covers composition events, native flags, Safari-style 229, both Enter-to-generate settings, and an actual open mention dropdown. Focused jsdom proof uses browser-layout polyfills plus visual/settings/unopened-subtree seams; the component and keyboard/dropdown handlers are real. Full Nx/Tauri builds and a real OS IME were not run. No generation or account calls were made.

AI-assisted implementation, verified with native regression tests.

Independent review replayed all eight tests from the exact signed commit in a separate worktree. A fresh paginated file audit of all 33 open PRs found no MentionTextarea overlap.

The existing batch has failed Netlify docs deploy previews; their authenticated build logs are unavailable to this account, and diagnostics were requested on #2069. These checks are not reported as passing.

title: fix(video-editor): finish pending saves before project exit
author: rudycelekli
body:
## What changed

Finish an existing autosave before flushing the latest dirty snapshot, and make concurrent flush callers wait for the active write. If exit saving fails, keep the editor and its active project available, show the existing error toast, and re-enable exit so the user can retry. Navigate only after saving and closing succeeds.

## Why

The editor header awaits `project.prepareExit()`, which awaits `save.flush()`. Previously `saveNow()` returned immediately when an autosave was in flight, allowing the editor to close before a later edit was persisted. The header also navigated in a `finally` block after saving failed, preventing a useful retry. This PR fixes the complete exit/save failure path together.

## Verification

- Save manager: three regression failures and one passing ordinary-flush control before the fix; all four tests pass afterward.
- Actual editor header: failure/retry regression fails on the preceding commit, while ordinary-success and pending-double-click controls pass; all three pass after the follow-up.
- Independently replayed all seven tests from the final signed head in a separate review worktree using Vitest 3.2.6.
- Real mounted `EditorHeader`, `ProjectManager.prepareExit`/`closeProject`, `SaveManager` and serialization execute with controlled delayed/failing host storage writes.

## Limits

Host hooks/navigation, visual widgets, unopened dialogs and unused media/settings imports are test seams. Full Nx/Tauri builds, native routing and actual filesystem persistence were not run.

Netlify docs preview diagnostics require authentication and have been requested on #2069. No hosted check is claimed green.

AI-assisted implementation with native regression tests and independent review replay. The save/header follow-up is included in this PR rather than submitted separately.

title: fix(grok,fal): don't hold std lock across await; poll FAL tasks concurrently
author: HighTecno
body:
Addresses two of the small items from #2065 (section 4).

## Changes

- **`GrokWrappedWebsocket`**: `send`, `get_response_with_timeout` and `try_next_timeout` held a `std::sync::RwLock` write guard across `.await` (clippy `await_holding_lock`). That can block the runtime or deadlock. Replaced with `tokio::sync::Mutex`.

`reset_artcraft_command` (unregistered Tauri command, also from #2065) is left for a maintainer to decide whether to wire up or remove.

title: fix(gallery): ignore responses superseded by a reset
author: rudycelekli
body:
## Problem

The desktop image, video and audio create pages use `useGalleryData` for completed history. Resetting the hook for a username/filter change or refresh releases its in-flight loading guard, but does not invalidate the previous request. An older response can therefore replace the refreshed feed or clear the loading flags of the newer request.

## Change

Track ownership of the current history load. Invalidate old responses on resets, refreshes and cleanup; only the current generation may apply results or release loading flags. Also clear the loading state when the username becomes unavailable. Preserve ordinary pagination and concurrent-load protection.

## Validation

Mounted the real React hook with real GalleryModalApi/MediaFilesApi/ApiManager response decoding and thumbnail mapping, using deferred fetch responses. The unchanged regression suite had four failures and two passing controls on the original source; all six pass with this patch. Coverage includes older responses finishing first or last, refreshing in flight, clearing an unavailable username, ordinary pagination and failed current requests. `git diff --check` passes.

The focused runtime transparently replaces the Tauri FetchProxy transport with controlled global fetch. No live backend, account, full Nx build or Tauri integration was exercised. Old network requests are ignored rather than cancelled.

AI assistance was used to investigate, implement and verify this change.

Independent review replayed the six tests from the exact signed commit in a separate worktree. The production files in this patch are unchanged between its base and current upstream main. A fresh complete open-PR file inventory found no overlapping useGalleryData change.

Existing Netlify docs previews are failing and require authenticated build diagnostics; logs were requested on #2069. No hosted check is claimed green.

title: fix(worldlabs): enqueue worlds as GaussianGeneration and notify frontend on completion
author: HighTecno

title: fix(promptbox): preserve current media references across async completion
author: rudycelekli
body:
## Problem

Pending reference uploads and library selections can commit against stale lists. Removing a reference during a video upload or metadata probe restores the removed item when that operation finishes. Independent completions can overwrite one another. The audio library path has the same snapshot problem, and audio uploads can overwrite each other when callbacks finish before the next render.

The desktop video prompt uses this hook and exposes removal of existing references during uploads.

## Change

Use the latest committed video/audio arrays for both local upload and asynchronous library-selection completion. Synchronize them and caller-provided count/duration limits in a layout effect, then update the shared ref immediately when publishing additions. This preserves edits and other completions before the next render. Recheck current limits after metadata probing and at upload commit; release the rejected upload preview if capacity has been filled meanwhile.

## Validation

The unchanged mounted-hook suite has fourteen failures and four passing controls on the original source; all eighteen pass with this patch. The initial upload-only candidate still had ten failures in that expanded suite, so its library/synchronization/limit gaps were repaired in this same change.

Coverage includes removal during upload/library metadata loading, upload and library completions overlapping, completions before the next render, a removal committed before passive effects, changed caller limits while work is pending, ordinary sequential batches, normal library selections, and count/duration capacity. Tests use native video/audio metadata events with controlled duration values and pending uploader callbacks. `git diff --check` passes.

No actual media decoding, network upload, live account or full Nx/Tauri build was run. The library-selection handler is exercised through the unopened gallery component's props; gallery/download/toast views and object URL methods are test seams…

title: fix(video-editor): preserve live media URLs across undo
author: rudycelekli
body:
## Problem

Undoing a multi-asset deletion can restore revoked object URLs. Each removal command saves the whole media array. Undo recreates a valid URL for its own asset, but a later undo replaces the whole array with an older snapshot containing the already-revoked URL of another restored asset. The same problem occurs with consecutive individual removals.

The asset bin calls the real `MediaManager.removeMediaAssets` path; this leaves restored media unreadable despite appearing in the bin.

## Change

Restore only the removed asset into the current media list at its saved position. Preserve the other assets' current object URLs. Existing revocation on removal and track restoration remain in place, and redo refreshes each removal's snapshot.

## Verification

- Native regression suite on original current-main implementation: three failures and one passing single-removal control.
- Fixed signed commit: all four tests pass. A separate worktree independently reproduced the before/after results.
- Actual `MediaManager`, `CommandManager`, `BatchCommand` and `RemoveMediaAssetCommand` execute. Tests read original file contents through real Node `File`, `URL.createObjectURL` and `fetch`; there is no simulated URL registry.
- Supplemental independent probes covered all fifteen nonempty ordered removal subsets with three undo/redo cycles and preservation of an additional live asset: sixteen more probes passed. The committed suite contains the four focused regression/control tests.
- Complete current open-PR file inventory found no overlapping removal-command change.

## Limits

The fixture has an empty timeline. The core singleton, rendering caches and unused waveform/ripple/element-construction imports are test seams. These tests establish readable file handles and list restoration, not actual video decoding, browser playback or full Nx/Tauri execution. Thumbnail behavior is unchanged.

Existing Netlify docs previews are failing; authenticated build diagnostics have been r…

title: fix(promptbox): stop reference audio when its owner disappears
author: rudycelekli
body:
## Problem

Audio reference previews outlive the tile that owns them. Removing a playing reference, unmounting the row, or replacing a reference URL leaves the detached HTMLAudioElement playing with no Stop control. A rejected play() promise from an earlier preview also resets the current preview's control after a user stops and starts another track.

The retained desktop callers are PromptBoxAudio and PageAudio/CreateAudio.

## Change

- Pause the owned element and clear its ended handler on URL replacement or unmount.
- Clear ownership before stopping playback.
- Ignore ended/rejected-play callbacks from elements that no longer own the tile.
- Add lifecycle and delayed-promise regressions through the mounted AudioReferenceRow.

## Verification

On current main 28a39a0, the focused suite reproduces four failures while three controls pass. The patch passes all seven tests, independently replayed in a second worktree. Controls cover normal stop/restart, the current track ending, and rejection of the current playback.

The focused Vitest 3.2.6/React/jsdom harness uses real mounted components and HTMLAudioElements; play/pause hardware methods are controlled spies, and icon/toast imports use presentation seams. This proves pause dispatch and callback/control ownership, not audible OS playback. No full Nx/Tauri build is claimed; the current machine has insufficient space for that build.

## Assistance

Prepared with AI assistance; the production diff and before/after regression results were independently reviewed before submission.

title: fix(video-editor): keep delayed media imports in their initiating context
author: rudycelekli
body:
## What changed

Keep delayed media imports bound to their initiating editor context. Clipboard imports now require the same project and scene and a mounted listener before running commands. The shared media manager and add-media command enforce their supplied project IDs; command undo also respects ownership. File/gallery completion counts include only registrations accepted by the manager.

## Why

Switching project or scene while an upload resolves could add the previous paste's media and clips to the new editor context. File/gallery imports passed a project ID that the manager discarded. Unmounting removed the paste listener but left its pending operation able to mutate the editor.

## Verification

- Eleven focused tests: seven ownership regressions fail before this patch while four controls pass; all eleven pass after it.
- Mounted React hook with actual media processor, toast, media/history commands and placement, plus delayed adapter upload/resolve.
- Cases cover project/scene switching, unmount, shared manager ownership, duplicate IDs, command execute/undo, optional-ID compatibility and internal clipboard paste.
- `git diff --check` passes.

Synthetic video decoding, WASM time conversion, adapter context and singleton access are explicit test seams. No native media decode, full desktop/CDN integration or full frontend build is claimed. Completed host uploads are retained; this patch does not delete durable host-library assets when the initiating context changes.

AI assistance was used to investigate the ownership race, implement the change and prepare the regression tests.

title: fix(video-editor): close IndexedDB connections after settled operations
author: rudycelekli
body:
## Problem
The live video editor uses the default IndexedDB project-storage adapter. Every operation opens a connection, but the transaction helper never closes it. Native save/load/list operations leave completed connections open, which can block a later database version upgrade; failure paths leak the same ownership.

## Change
Close the connection in the transaction promise finalizer. Results, transaction completion and public storage methods retain their behavior. Add a standalone native-browser regression harness and exact reproduction instructions without new dependencies. The harness routes to its own test database and uses WeakRef tracking rather than retaining database objects.

## Verification
Real isolated Chrome154 native IndexedDB: upstream fails four cleanup/upgrade cases and passes two round-trip controls; this patch passes all six. Cases include native structured-clone failure and native transaction.abort(), not fake-IDB. Only the actual adapter is transpiled; no full build is needed. Generated browser profiles measured below3MB and were deleted after process exit.

Chrome proof does not establish Tauri/WebKit compatibility or passing hosted/full-suite checks.

AI assistance was used to investigate, implement, and verify the change.

title: fix(video-editor): persist active scene after deletion and undo
author: rudycelekli
body:
## Summary

Deleting the selected scene updates the editor's active scene but leaves the project document's `currentSceneId` pointing to the deleted scene. Undo after switching scenes also restores the active scene without restoring the persisted selection.

Keep the stored scene selection synchronized with the scene manager when scene commands replace the scene list. This covers deletion, undo and redo together.

## Verification

- Real scene/project/command managers and document serialization: frozen main produces three regression failures and three passing controls; the fix passes all six.
- Covers selected-scene deletion, undo after switching scenes, redo, unselected deletion, ordinary switch/rename, and protected main-scene deletion.
- The tests isolate unrelated renderer/audio initialization, unused bookmark/ripple/time paths and media downloads. Storage captures a JSON roundtrip of the actual serialized document.
- `git diff --check` passes. Full desktop/Nx build and browser integration were not run.

AI assistance was used to investigate, implement and verify this change.

title: fix(settings): keep provider order after cancelled or stale drops
author: rudycelekli
body:
## Problem
Dropping a provider outside all targets produced a null `over`, but the pane converted its missing ID to array index -1 and moved the dragged provider to the end. The changed priority was persisted even though no valid reorder was requested. Stale active or target IDs likewise selected an unintended item.

## Change
Ignore null targets and same-item drops. Require both IDs to exist in the current state before moving or persisting provider priorities. Valid reorders retain their behavior.

## Verification
Three regressions fail on main while two controls pass; all five mounted React tests pass after the change. An independent worktree reproduced the same before/after result. Tests exercise the actual pane and locked @dnd-kit/sortable 10.0.0 arrayMove implementation. Drag-end delivery, visual wrappers and Tauri persistence are controlled boundaries; no physical pointer hit-testing, live provider or full desktop build is claimed. Diff check passes.

AI assistance was used to investigate, implement and verify this change.

title: fix(video-editor): preserve visible thumbnails for very thin images
author: rudycelekli
body:
## What changed

Keep at least one pixel in each thumbnail dimension when scaling a valid positive, finite image. Existing calculations and behavior for invalid dimensions remain unchanged.

## Why

Valid very thin PNGs import into the editor but thumbnail rounding can create a zero-sized canvas. Its `data:,` result is not a decodable image, leaving the media preview blank.

## Verification

- Thirteen sizing tests: original source fails two thin-image cases and passes eleven controls; this patch passes all thirteen, including invalid-dimension parity.
- Native Chrome PNG encoding/Image decoding through the actual media processor and public local-file adapter reproduces the original two failures and four controls.
- Independent exact-commit replay: original source fails two native PNG import cases while four controls pass; corrected source passes all six native cases. Independent sizing replay also passes all thirteen tests.
- `git diff --check` passes and the commit is signed.

Native browser proof does not establish Tauri/WebKit/CDN integration or a passing full frontend build. No Image/Canvas/encoder mocks are used; the unused video branch is outside these tests. AI assistance was used for investigation, patching and regression preparation.

title: fix(video-editor): end property scrubbing when its field disappears
author: rudycelekli
body:
## Summary

A property scrub registers document pointer listeners that currently survive the field being removed. Subsequent pointer movement can keep previewing edits through the removed field's callback. Escape releasing pointer lock or losing window focus also leaves the scrub alive.

Give each scrub an owned, idempotent cleanup path. Remove its listeners when the field disappears or the interaction ends, release only its own pointer lock, and avoid committing through an unmounted field. Ordinary scrubbing still commits once.

## Verification

- Actual mounted `NumberField`: frozen main fails four lifecycle/ownership cases and passes two controls; fixed head passes all six.
- Covers removal during drag, pointer-lock loss, window blur, another control's lock, ordinary drag completion, disabled/non-primary input.
- Pointer-lock API ownership is a controlled test seam; this does not claim native OS capture or full desktop integration. Icons, class names and unused reset-button rendering are isolated.
- `git diff --check` passes. No full desktop/Nx build was run.

AI assistance was used to investigate, implement and verify the change.

title: fix(generation-list): prevent obsolete polls from restoring completed jobs
author: rudycelekli
body:
## Summary

The audio page's generation feed polls every five seconds and refreshes when the task queue changes. Responses can finish out of order: an older pending-job response can replace a newer completed-job response, bringing back the pending card. An obsolete response can also finish expanding completed media after a later poll, or update the feed after its effect is disabled or its media filter changes.

Track request order separately from effect ownership. Commit a response only if its effect still owns the feed and it is newer than the last committed response. Check again after asynchronous media expansion, before changing completion/failure tracking or emitting credit events. A newer request merely being pending does not block a valid response, so slow connections continue to make progress.

## Verification

- Frozen main: four failing regression cases and three passing controls. Fixed code: all seven pass.
- Actual mounted hook, React/DOM task-queue events, production JobsApi/MediaFilesApi/ApiManager JSON decoding, native Response objects, actual JobStatus and thumbnail helpers. The FetchProxy transport and model display metadata are controlled seams; no external backend or full desktop run is claimed.
- Cases cover reversed response order, changed media filter, disabled polling, superseded batch expansion, normal completion, initial historic-completion suppression, and progress with newer requests still pending.
- Independent review additionally checks the real five-second timer and stale/current credit-event behavior: five failures/five controls before; ten passing cases after. It caught and rejected an initial guard that would starve slow polls.
- git diff --check passes. No full Nx/Tauri build was run.

AI assistance was used to investigate, implement and verify this change.

title: fix(video-editor): retain replacement waveform requests after stale failures
author: rudycelekli
body:
## Summary

An in-flight waveform request can outlive `clearSource` or `clearAll`. If another request for the same source is cached and the old request then fails, the old catch handler currently deletes the replacement cache entry. The next consumer starts a duplicate download instead of joining the replacement request.

Evict a failed request only while it still owns that source's cache entry. Keep retrying ordinary current-request failures as before.

## Verification

title: Fix native model picker flyout closing when the pointer leaves the family row
author: mikekuriger
body:
**Problem:** In `artcraft-native`, clicking a family in the model picker opens a flyout of its variants, but the flyout disappears as soon as the pointer leaves the family row, so variants can't be selected.

**Cause:** the hovered family was stored in egui temp data as `Option<String>` but read back as `String`, so it never persisted and the flyout only showed while the row itself was hovered.

**Changes**
- Read the hovered family back with the type it was stored as.
- Add a small hover bridge around the flyout so crossing the gap between the row and the flyout doesn't dismiss it.
- The main popup ignores clicks, and closes only on clicks outside the popup, the pill and open flyouts. Previously a click inside a flyout counted as outside and closed the popup before the pick landed.
- `pickers::popover_with` takes the close behavior, and `popover` delegates to it unchanged.

**Testing:** `cargo test -p artcraft_native` passes (62 passed), and I checked the fix by hand in the running app.

title: Fix flatpak unresponsiveness for ArtCraft Launcher
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
# Fix Flatpak unresponsiveness for ArtCraft Launcher

## Problem
The `ai.storyteller.artcraft-launcher` flatpak becomes unresponsive due to:
1. Missing D-Bus service permissions causing the app to hang on `do_epoll_wait`
2. Development artifacts left in the binary causing sandbox conflicts  
3. Missing cleanup section in flatpak manifest

## Root Cause Analysis
The app logs show:
```
[2026-10-12T04:26:17Z WARN  artcraft_launcher] no tray icon: D-Bus connection error: org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.ServiceUnknown: org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.ServiceUnknown
```

The app tries to:

- Use D-Bus services for notifications
- Access GPU resources via DRI

Added missing D-Bus services:
- `--own-name=ai.storyteller.artcraft-launcher` - Register own bus name
- `--own-name=ai.artcraft.app` - Tauri app identifier  
- `--talk-name=org.freedesktop.DBus` - D-Bus system access
- `--talk-name=org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierWatcher` - Alternative tray icon service
- Additional desktop environment services

### 2. Cleanup development artifacts
Added `cleanup` section to remove:
- Debug symbols (`*.debug`, `*.pdb`)
- Development files (`/usr/include`, `/usr/lib/debug`)
- Build system files

### 3. Binary stripping
Added `strip --strip-unneeded` to remove unnecessary symbols

### 4. Environment variables
Added essential environment variables for:
- X11/Wayland display
- D-Bus session bus
- XDG runtime directory

## Testing
Before fix:
- App hangs in `do_epoll_wait` state
- Unable to connect to D-Bus services
- Window never appears

After fix:
- ✓ App launches successfully
- ✓ D-Bus connections work
- ✓ GPU access via DRI

- `flatpak/manifest.json` - Enhanced permissions, cleanup, stripping
- `flatpak/README.md` - Build instructions

- Maintains all existing functionality

title: fix (login-modal) : validate signup fields before submitting
author: Ridzzz0Alam
body:
## Summary

The desktop signup form only checked that the two passwords matched. Everything else went straight to `/v1/create_account` and came back as an HTTP 400. With the error formatting in v0.41.0 that showed up as `Login server rejected the request (HTTP Some(400))` which is what users are reporting.

#2025 already turns server rejections into readable messages. This PR catches the common mistakes in the form before any request is made.

## Problems fixed

- **Invalid usernames reached the server.** Usernames shorter than 3 or longer than 16 characters or with spaces or symbols are now rejected in the form.
- **Short passwords reached the server.** Passwords under 6 characters are now rejected in the form.

- **The placeholder disagreed with the server.** The password field said "Min. 8 characters" while the server message says 6. It now reads from one constant.
- **Old errors stayed on screen.** After "Passwords do not match.", fixing the passwords and resubmitting left the red banner up while the request ran. The error now clears on every submit.

The new messages use the same wording as `password_auth_error_message.rs`, so a mistake reads the same whether the form or the server catches it. Email format is left to the existing `type="email"` input.

title: fix(frontend): handle localStorage access errors to prevent mount failure (#1984)
author: gabrieelibrahim
body:
## Summary
Closes #1984.

Safely handle `localStorage` access errors (`SecurityError` / `DOMException`) across initial component render and state handlers:
- **TaskQueue.tsx**: Guard `localStorage.getItem("taskQueueLastReadAt")` in `useState` initializer and `localStorage.setItem` in `handleOpenChange`.
- **index.tsx**: Guard `localStorage.getItem("st-theme")` inside the initial theme mount effect.
- **ConfirmationModal.tsx**: Guard `localStorage.setItem` on dismiss check.

## Problem
In sandboxed webviews, strict privacy profiles, or environments where local storage is disabled, accessing `localStorage` throws a `SecurityError`. Because `TaskQueue.tsx` read `taskQueueLastReadAt` directly in the initial `useState` callback, the unhandled exception abruptly crashed the React render tree, causing the app to fail mounting and display a blank white screen (#1984).

## Solution
Wrap storage reads and writes in `try / catch`, falling back to default/absent values when storage access is denied so the frontend mounts cleanly without disrupting normal storage persistence.

An artist can finish an image in another application and explicitly hand the saved file to ArtCraft. This contribution adds a focused stdio MCP bridge to inspect selected PNG/JPEG files, import them, explain interrupted results, and verify an accepted asset's original bytes.

title: ci: skip stale storyteller-docs Netlify builds
author: channelramble
body:
## Problem
Every PR in this repo shows four failed `storyteller-docs` checks (`deploy-preview`, Header rules, Redirect rules, Pages changed). The deploy log shows the build fails before building anything:

```
No config file was defined: using default values.
bash: line 1: ./script/netlify_build_docs.sh: No such file or directory
  In Build command from Netlify app:
  ./script/netlify_build_docs.sh
```

That script and the docs moved to [storytold/artcraft-services](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft-services/blob/main/script/netlify_build_docs.sh), but the Netlify site is still connected to this repository.

## Fix
Add a root `netlify.toml` whose `ignore` command exits 0, which tells Netlify to skip the build. This only affects the `storyteller-docs` site (the only Netlify site reporting checks here).

The proper long-term fix is on the Netlify side: repoint `storyteller-docs` at artcraft-services or disconnect it from this repo, then delete this file. This PR just stops every contributor's PR from being marked failed in the meantime.

## Testing
This PR's own checks are the test: Netlify reads `netlify.toml` from the PR head, so its deploy preview should be skipped instead of failing.

title: Fix FAL queue client after deserialization
author: legendteddy
body:
Summary

Restore a usable HTTP client when a serialized FAL "Queue" is deserialized.

Previously, the "client" field was skipped by serde and became "None". Calling "status()", "response()", or "cancel()" on the restored queue then unwrapped that missing client and panicked.

This change:

- recreates the reqwest client during deserialization;
- removes the "Option"/"unwrap()" path from queue operations;
- adds a regression test that round-trips a queue through JSON and exercises status, response, and cancellation against a local HTTP fixture.

Addresses item 3 of #2270.

title: Fix native library retry after initial load failure
author: legendteddy
body:
Allow the native generation feed to retry its first library page after a transient load failure.

Previously, "next_library_page()" marked the library as started before the request completed. If page 0 failed, "library_failed()" only cleared the loading flag, leaving the store in a started state with "has_more == false". Subsequent visits therefore treated the library as finished and never retried.

This change:

- clears the initial "library_started" state when page 0 fails;
- preserves existing state for failures on later pages;
- adds regression tests covering both initial-page and later-page retry behavior.

Addresses item 1 of #2269.

title: Add Craft AI: the family's built-in local assistant (Gemma 4, optional, shared, private)
author: hasan-sdaif
body:
## What this is

**Craft AI** — one assistant across the ArtCraft family, as a page in ArtCraft. It talks to a
local model runtime on this machine and never to a cloud service:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Local and private** | Every request is `http://127.0.0.1` — Ollama (11434), LM Studio (1234) or llama.cpp's server (8080), whichever answers. No account, no key, no telemetry, and no address a cloud service could be reached at exists in the code. |
| **Light by design** | No inference engine, no weights, no GPU code enters the app. The runtime the user already has (or installs) does the running — Craft AI is a loopback conversation. |
| **Optional** | Without a runtime or a model the page says so and touches nothing beyond loopback. Downloading is a button, never a default. |
| **A page beside the makers** | ArtCraft's image, video and audio making stay exactly what they are — the cloud generators the app is built on. Craft AI is the family's assistant beside them: the local, private one that helps you *use* them — write and polish the prompt, pick a style direction, name the piece. |
| **Specialised** | The system prompt tells the model it is inside ArtCraft and names this app's world — prompts, style directions, the pieces in the library — so the ready-made tasks (write a prompt, polish a prompt, style ideas, name this piece) come back about this app's work. |
| **One download serves every app** | The model file lands in a shared folder the whole family reads — `<data_home>/ArtCraft/Craft AI/models` — so a model downloaded here is already there in every other ArtCraft app, no second download. Ollama's own store works the same way machine-wide. |

## The three tabs

- **Assistant** — runtime and model pickers, the task, the question, the answer; the conversation is kept and copyable, and Arabic answers are drawn through the same visual-order pass as the rest of the interface. Worker thread, so the UI never blocks; a busy timer ticks while the model thinks.
- **Models** —…

title: fix(video-editor): retain pending saves after failures
author: euisuh
body:
A rejected project write currently clears the pending-save flag, so the manager reports clean after a failed flush. Timer-triggered failures also escape as unhandled rejections.

Keep the failed save pending and preserve explicit flush errors. Timer saves log their failures; a later edit, flush or resume retries. Failed writes do not start an automatic retry loop, while edits made during successful writes retain their existing debounced follow-up.

Closes #2313

Validation:

- Regression tests against unchanged main: 3 failures, 1 pass, 1 unhandled rejection.
- Fixed: all 5 new SaveManager tests and 5 existing serialization tests pass using the existing Vite config.
- Scoped repository ESLint and `git diff --check` pass. Nx module-boundary checking skipped because no project graph was available.
- Full library collection remains blocked by missing `culori`; library typecheck encounters missing application modules (first `zustand`), and spec typecheck requires unbuilt library declarations. Full desktop/frontend CI and real IndexedDB failures were not exercised.

Related #2077 addresses waiting for in-flight saves during project exit. This patch only preserves failed saves and handles timer rejection; it uses a separate test filename to reduce overlap.

CI integration repair: the first preview failed with exit 127 because Netlify still invokes the removed `script/netlify_build_docs.sh`. Added the same conditional `netlify.toml` guard reviewed in #2275: skip only while the legacy script is absent. Parsed TOML and both absent/restored-script exit paths pass. This skips obsolete documentation deployment; it does not test the application or repoint the Netlify site.

title: fix(sqlite_tasks): preserve task storage on startup errors
author: channelramble
body:
SQLite startup currently unlinks the task database after any connection or migration error. A lock or migration checksum mismatch can therefore erase pending jobs and history.

Return the original error and preserve storage. Explicitly close the pool when migrations fail so SQLite handles are released before a retry, including on Windows. Recovery is now non-destructive; an incompatible database requires deliberate recovery instead of an automatic reset.

Closes #2249.

Validation: four real SQLx integration tests pass for new/reopened storage, checksum failure and recovery, invalid-file preservation, and a database locked by another connection. Against unchanged main, the three preservation regressions fail. Tests ran on macOS; Windows was not exercised. `git diff --check` passes.

Includes the unchanged Netlify guard from #2248 as a separate commit, because the obsolete storyteller-docs integration otherwise fails every submission. Remove that commit from the diff once #2248 lands.

title: fix(tasks): preserve cancellation and record transition timestamps
author: channelramble
body:
A provider response arriving after local cancellation currently changes the task back to success/failure. Completion timestamps also remain unset, and unrelated providers cannot reuse the same job ID.

Add a forward SQLite migration that preserves terminal statuses, records transition/completion timestamps atomically, and scopes job-ID uniqueness to its provider (retaining uniqueness for legacy NULL-provider rows). Rejected transitions report zero affected rows. ArtCraft polling skips terminal tasks, and ArtCraft, FAL, and classic Sora failure handlers emit events only after a successful state change; completion handlers already check the update result.

Closes #2262.

Validation:
- Six SQLx integration tests pass: cancellation followed by late success/failure, every terminal state, retryable failure followed by success, stable metadata/timestamps, provider ID collisions, legacy NULL-provider uniqueness, and migration of existing history. Without the migration, five tests fail.
- Desktop test target compiles with `SQLX_OFFLINE=true cargo test -p artcraft --lib --no-run` (existing warnings).
- `git diff --check` passes.

Cancellation remains local abandonment; this does not abort provider requests or downloads already in flight, and existing unknown completion times are not backfilled. Windows and live-provider flows were not exercised.

Includes the unchanged Netlify guard from #2248 as a separate commit so the obsolete documentation integration does not fail this submission. The related non-destructive SQLite startup fix is #2360.

title: fix(canvas): route Flux inpainting and surface submission failures
author: channelramble
body:
Canvas selects `flux_pro_1` for Flux Pro inpainting, but the ArtCraft dispatcher sends it to Omni as text-to-image model `FluxPro11`. A rejected request then escapes Canvas generation without a visible error.

Route Flux Pro inpainting through the existing dedicated `/v1/generate/image/inpaint/flux_pro_1` endpoint, preserving the source, normalized mask, prompt, batch size, and inpaint task identity. Remove the incorrect Omni model mapping. Canvas now catches submission failures, displays the error, releases the Generate button for retry, and adds pending history only after success. The synchronous duplicate-submission guard is preserved.

Closes #2279.

Validation:
- Six Rust tests pass in the compiled desktop library: routing/model mapping plus source/mask validation, source precedence, payload preservation, and batch limits. Both routing regressions fail with the original mapping/dispatch restored.
- All eight PageDraw Vitest tests pass, including six new failure/retry/concurrent-submission cases.
- The new hook and tests pass strict TypeScript checking and scoped ESLint (Nx module-boundary rule skips without a project graph).
- `git diff --check` passes. Full PageDraw typechecking is blocked by unbuilt workspace declaration references; the existing PageDraw file also has unrelated lint errors. Live paid generation and Windows were not exercised.

Includes the unchanged Netlify guard from #2248 as a separate commit to avoid the obsolete storyteller-docs deployment failure.

title: Bound API polling requests and end disconnected Midjourney streams
author: channelramble
body:
Polling can stop making progress when an ArtCraft HTTP response stalls or a Midjourney socket disappears while a handle remains alive. Shared API requests now use a 10-second connection deadline and 30-second total deadline; the five multipart upload entry points retain a 10-minute total budget.

Midjourney job streams now observe driver shutdown independently of the broadcast sender, report lost events instead of waiting for a possibly discarded completion, and drain queued completion events before reporting disconnect. Sending a close frame ends the driver as documented.

Addresses the shared HTTP deadline and WebSocket lifecycle portions of #2270. The separate FAL queue response work is tracked by #2307; this PR does not close the whole audit.

Validation: two loopback HTTP tests exercise stalled headers and stalled response bodies using the production 30-second deadline, then verify a healthy next request. Three channel lifecycle tests cover retained handles, lost completion events, and completion immediately before disconnect. All five pass. `cargo check --offline -p artcraft_client` passes. No live provider jobs were submitted.

Includes the unchanged `netlify.toml` guard from #2248 so the obsolete documentation site does not reject this desktop PR. A successful Netlify check reflects that intentional skip, not application test coverage.

title: Respect cookie scope when importing the native ArtCraft session
author: channelramble
body:
The native app imported cookies by searching for `storyteller.ai` inside a serialized domain. That could select a different host's session, ignore path restrictions, or carry production credentials into a localhost configuration.

Parse the Tauri cookie jar using its existing RFC cookie-store format and select credentials for the configured API root URL. This preserves host-only, domain, path, Secure and expiry semantics. Reject ambiguous duplicate session or visitor cookies instead of choosing an arbitrary identity.

Fixes #2260.

Validation: `cargo test -p artcraft_native cookie_import_tests` passes all three fixture tests (exact/parent domains, lookalike and unrelated hosts, host-only scope, restricted paths, expired cookies, and production versus localhost). The native test target compiles. No real credentials were read by these tests. Existing native session-file account/host migration is outside this import fix.

Includes the unchanged Netlify submission guard from #2248; obsolete docs deploys are intentionally skipped.

title: Recover native previews, audio loads, and recreated video keyframes
author: channelramble
body:
Native previews can remain broken after a transient download error, and recreating a video can silently change how its images are submitted. This fixes five independent state/lifetime defects from #2271:

- Recreated prompts restore keyframe versus reference mode from their saved semantics and place explicit start/end frames correctly regardless of list order.
- Failed still/animated image previews become retryable after a five-second cooldown, with repaint scheduling.
- Failed audio waveforms use the same cooldown instead of remaining permanently failed.
- Audio downloads carry a request identity, so stopping and restarting the same URL cannot accept an older success or error.
- Attached local image references retain their source bytes. The texture cache holds weak references and can decode them again after eviction; removing the attachment releases its source, including character reference uploads.

Validation: the full native suite passes (68 tests, one existing FFmpeg integration test ignored). Six new regression tests exercise request serialization, stale audio results, cooldown behavior, actual local PNG decoding after cache eviction, and source release. No live generation was requested. This addresses these five findings, not the entire #2271 audit.

Includes the unchanged Netlify guard from #2248 so the obsolete documentation deployment is skipped.

title: Bound native video memory and stop abandoned or failing subprocesses
author: channelramble
body:
Native playback could buffer an entire decoded soundtrack, continuously respawn failing video decoders, and leave a blocked ffprobe running after the lightbox closed.

Bound the PCM queue to four 8 KiB chunks with backpressure, and stop its sink when the stream is dropped. Loop a video only after a successful decoder exit that produced frames; failed or empty decodes now show an error. The probe worker owns and reaps its child, responds to cancellation when the player closes, and enforces a 30-second deadline. Probe failure/termination also leaves the loading state.

Fixes #2267.

Validation on macOS: four video unit/regression tests pass, including full-queue backpressure, receiver shutdown, failed/empty decoders, and real subprocess cancellation/timeout with process-exit checks. The existing ignored FFmpeg integration test was explicitly run and passes: it generates, probes, seeks and decodes a real clip. Windows subprocess behavior was not exercised.

Includes the unchanged Netlify guard from #2248 for the obsolete documentation deployment.

title: Serialize provider credential cache loads with saves and deletion
author: channelramble
body:
A cache miss could read an old credential file, then insert that stale value after another thread deleted or replaced it. Keep each disk read/cache insertion, save/cache update, and delete/invalidation under the shared write lock, with a cache recheck after lock acquisition.

Addresses the generic cache portion of #2257. Independently loaded Midjourney managers and interprocess ownership remain outside this change.

Validation: two deterministic interleaving tests pause a disk load and race deletion/replacement; both pass. The combined credential suite passes 25 tests on macOS, including the existing API-key serialization tests.

Includes the unchanged Netlify guard from #2248 so the obsolete documentation deployment is intentionally skipped.

title: Remove auxiliary Grok and WorldLabs credentials when disconnecting
author: channelramble
body:
Disconnect removed only the main provider state, leaving raw Grok cookies and WorldLabs cookies/bearer/refresh tokens behind. The credential managers now remove every owned representation while holding their state lock, and persistence retains that lock through file writes so an earlier snapshot cannot restore cleared files. Persisting an empty manager no longer recreates the state file.

Addresses the Grok/WorldLabs portion of #2255. Other providers are untouched.

Validation: two temporary-directory regressions verify all owned files disappear, repeated clearing succeeds, empty persistence does not recreate them, and unrelated provider files remain. Both pass in the 25-test combined credential run; the desktop library test target compiles.

Includes the unchanged Netlify guard from #2248 so the obsolete documentation deployment is intentionally skipped.

title: Purge ArtCraft sessions from the authoritative HTTP cookie jar
author: channelramble
body:
ArtCraft logout cleared manager and webview copies but left the HTTP-plugin jar available to the recurring credential synchronizer. Purge now removes session/visitor cookies for the configured API domain (including scoped paths), clears manager/disk copies under the same jar lock used by synchronization, and awaits persistence before clearing the webview.

HTTP jar saves are serialized and snapshot current state only when they acquire the writer lock. A queued older save can no longer overwrite a completed purge with its earlier snapshot. Unrelated cookies are preserved.

Addresses the ArtCraft HTTP-jar portion of #2255. This is local credential removal, not server-side token revocation; an independent future authentication response can still install new cookies.

Validation: a fixture queues a save, purges without any server logout, waits for that earlier save, reloads disk, and runs synchronization again. It verifies no session returns, path-scoped cookies are gone, and unrelated cookies survive. All 16 login bridge tests pass on macOS, including a new cleanup-failure regression that verifies the authoritative jar is still flushed. A deterministic plugin test holds the writer lock to prove a queued save snapshots only after acquiring it; that test passes too. The earlier combined credential suite passed 25 tests. Login persistence now awaits an uncancellable flush, and webview cleanup is attempted even if another cleanup step fails.

Includes the unchanged Netlify guard from #2248 so the obsolete documentation deployment is intentionally skipped.

title: Write API keys and native sessions atomically with private Unix permissions
author: channelramble
body:
Tauri API keys, native sessions and native FAL keys used truncating writes and default permissions. Add a shared atomic replacement helper that writes/syncs a same-directory temporary file before replacing the destination; files are 0600 on Unix. Credential directory creation now explicitly uses/tightens 0700 for both desktop clients, without chmodding general-purpose parent directories.

Addresses #2256 for the three audited credential write paths. Existing credential directories are tightened on startup; legacy file modes are corrected when those files are replaced. Windows uses inherited directory access controls; explicit Windows ACL hardening is not implemented or claimed.

Validation: interrupted-write tests preserve the old value and remove the temporary file. A subprocess with umask 000 verifies new/replaced file modes and tightening an existing directory. Both helper tests pass, the native FAL save/mask/delete test passes, and the combined desktop credential suite passes 25 tests including existing API-key round trips.

Includes the unchanged Netlify guard from #2248 so the obsolete documentation deployment is intentionally skipped.

title: Resume FAL uploads with durable identities and clean transfer files
author: channelramble
body:
FAL completion retries generated fresh batch/upload identities and repeated already confirmed uploads. Downloaded transfer files also accumulated in the app's persistent temporary directory.

Persist the batch token and each result's idempotency token before uploading, checkpoint each confirmed media token, and resume only unfinished results after retry/restart. Explicit-idempotency bindings now cover video and legacy uploads as well as the existing image binding, including rate-limit retries. Database completion failure preserves the checkpoint; confirmed completion removes it. Changed result URL lists are rejected instead of silently associating old identities with different media.

Downloads now check HTTP status and have a finite timeout. Owned temporary files are deleted on normal success, failure, and cancellation unwinding. Existing abandoned files and abrupt-process-termination cleanup are not handled by this PR. User-requested auto-downloads remain separate.

Addresses the retry identity/progress and normal transfer-file lifecycle findings in #2263.

Validation: four desktop regression tests pass, including fail-second/restart recovery, stable identity after a lost response, skipping completed uploads after database failure, failing before upload when checkpoints cannot persist, real loopback multipart requests for all three media types, temporary file removal, and HTTP errors. `cargo check --offline -p artcraft_client` passes. No provider generation or real upload was requested; server-side deduplication beyond the supplied API token is not independently verified.

Includes the unchanged Netlify submission guard from #2248.

title: Validate native reference limits before image and video generation
author: channelramble
body:
Native image/video submission could retain references from a more permissive model or accept library clips whose combined duration exceeded the current model's limit. Validate the complete active reference input immediately before generation: counts, supported kinds, upload/token readiness, aggregate durations, and first/last-frame support.

Invalid input stays attached and an actionable error explains what to remove or reattach. References with unknown/nonfinite duration must be reattached from the library when a duration limit applies; they cannot silently bypass that limit.

Addresses the reference-validation portion of #2269. Initial library retry is separately covered by #2308.

Validation: the full native suite passes (65 tests, one existing FFmpeg test ignored). Three new regressions cover model limits changing 3→1→0 without silently deleting input, individually valid library clips exceeding an aggregate limit, unknown durations, and unready/unsupported keyframes. No live generation was requested.

Includes the unchanged Netlify submission guard from #2248.

title: Send 3D library assets and generated results to the stage
author: channelramble
body:
The library lightbox already had an optional scene callback, but the desktop never supplied it. Wire it to a **Send to stage** action for saved 3D meshes/splats, and reuse that action for generated 3D results.

The transfer switches to the 3D tab, waits for both the editor and its saved scene to finish loading, and awaits actual object creation. Duplicate clicks are blocked. Failures keep the viewer open, show an error, and permit retry; success closes the library viewer. Leaving the tab cancels a pending transfer. The existing 500 ms timer and unconditional success notification in generated results are removed.

Fixes #1030.

Validation: 18 app tests and 13 viewer tests pass. Seven new regressions cover delayed scene readiness, timeouts, missing media IDs, tab changes, rejected insertion, duplicate clicks, failure/retry, and success-only closing. ESLint passes for the new helper/button and their tests (Nx boundary rule disabled because this checkout has no project graph). A live Tauri/WebGL stage insertion and whole-workspace TypeScript build were not run.

Includes the unchanged Netlify submission guard from #2248.

title: Add PR regression CI, contributor guidance, and bug/feature forms
author: channelramble
body:
Add three pieces of contributor infrastructure:

- A read-only, secret-free regression workflow for pushes, pull requests and manual runs. It tests SQLite/cookie/API crates and the desktop/frontend 3D viewer suites on Linux. Actions are pinned to verified commit SHAs, installation uses the lockfiles, and jobs have concurrency cancellation and deadlines.
- A contribution guide and PR template describing reproduction, scoped issue references, relevant test commands, final-head submission checks, and the actual Netlify submission problem from #2248.
- Separate bug and feature forms that request app/platform/version/reproduction information or workflow/success criteria, while keeping blank issues available.

Addresses the missing-test-CI portion of #2273. This foundation does not claim whole-workspace type checking, linting, desktop release builds, or hotspot refactoring.

Validation locally on macOS: the exact Rust command passes 58 tests (live-provider/documentation tests remain ignored); the exact frontend commands pass 13 app and 11 viewer tests. Workflow and form YAML parses and its trigger/permission/field structure checks pass. Both jobs also passed on a clean Linux runner: https://github.com/channelramble/artcraft/actions/runs/38728273852. Upstream workflow approval, if required, remains a maintainer action.

Includes the unchanged `netlify.toml` guard from #2248. Its successful skip is explicitly distinguished from application test coverage in the guide.

title: Enforce HTTP permission scopes on every redirect
author: channelramble
body:
An allowed HTTP endpoint could redirect the vendored plugin to a destination outside its configured permissions. The redirect policy now checks the combined command/global allow and deny rules before each hop, while preserving the default redirect limit, custom limits, and `maxRedirections: 0` behavior.

Fixes #2259.

Validation: `cargo test -p tauri-plugin-http --lib` passed all 23 tests. Five real local-HTTP regressions cover denied origins (zero requests reach the destination), deny precedence, permitted redirects, disabled redirects, and redirect limits. No authenticated external services were contacted.

Includes the unchanged Netlify submission guard from #2248 because the obsolete docs deployment still points at this repository.

title: feat: digital-art pen (stylus) support — pressure, eraser tip, Linux XInput2 bridge
author: HuntedRaven7
body:
Windows/macOS consume standards-compliant pen PointerEvents directly in the
drawing surfaces (coalesced sampling, pressure, eraser tip, barrel pan), while
synthetic webview mouse events are suppressed to prevent double strokes.

On Linux, WebKitGTK flattens pen hardware to mouse events with hardcoded
pressure 0.5 (https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/issues/10636), so a native XInput2 reader (Rust,
runtime dlopen into libX11/libXi — no X11 dev headers or build-time pkg-config
required) relays real pen events to the webview over the "pen-event" channel.
Surfaces enable/disable capture refcount-style on mount/unmount.

- services/pen: XInput2 reader, refcounted capture state, camelCase event
  payload, enable/disable Tauri commands, reader thread spawned at startup

- lib.rs: manage Arc<PenCaptureState>, force GDK_BACKEND=x11 on Linux (only
  when unset and a DISPLAY exists) so GTK and the reader share one X server

- @storyteller/common pen.ts: shared channel name, pressure EMA smoothing,
  pressure-to-width mapping, eraser-tip detection, coalesced-event helper

- pagedraw: PressureStroke renderer (per-vertex tapered capsules) with live
  draw-time getters; LineNode gains optional pressures[]; PaintSurface
  integrates DOM pen events and the Linux bridge for draw/eraser/inpaint

- Storyboard SketchCanvas: pressure-tapered canvas strokes, eraser tip,
  pointercancel handling, Linux bridge listener

Known limitations: pen tilt/rotation not captured; Linux requires XWayland
(X11 backend); end-to-end event delivery must be validated on a real desktop
with a tablet (mock X servers deliver no XI2 event streams).

title: fix(dev): check Linux GTK/WebKit build dependencies
author: andresberejnoi
body:
> **Note:** I tried running Artcraft on Fedora and encountered some issues. I made some modifications using an LLM but I still tested these changes.

## Problem

On a fresh Linux setup, `./script/artcraft/unix_dev.sh` can fail while compiling `gobject-sys` (and other `*-sys` crates) with:

> The system library `gobject-2.0` ... was not found.
> The `PKG_CONFIG_PATH` environment variable is not set.

That message is misleading. The GTK/WebKit runtime libraries are installed, but the `-devel`/`-dev` packages that provide the pkg-config `.pc` files are not.

## Change

- Add `script/common/linux_preflight.sh`, which checks the required pkg-config modules before the Rust build and prints the correct install command for Fedora, Debian/Ubuntu, or Arch.
- Run it from `unix_dev.sh`, `unix_rust_dev.sh`, and `unix_build.sh`.
- Document the Linux development-package requirement in `_docs/dev_setup.md`.
- Skip the check in `unix-dev.test.mjs`, which uses a fake `cargo` and should run without system GTK/WebKit packages.

No package manager is invoked automatically. `ARTCRAFT_SKIP_SYSTEM_PREFLIGHT=1` bypasses the check for unusual setups.

## Related

- #2061 detects native toolchain requirements in the Windows Rust dev script; this is the Linux counterpart for system build dependencies.
- I did not find an existing open issue or PR covering the missing Linux GTK/WebKit `-devel` packages.

## Verification

- `bash -n` on all touched scripts
- Preflight passes with the development packages installed
- `node --test frontend/scripts/unix-dev.test.mjs` -> 7 passed, 0 failed
- Built and launched the desktop app locally on Fedora 43

title: fix(linux): use an opaque webview background
author: andresberejnoi
body:
> **Note:** I tried running Artcraft on Fedora and encountered some issues. I made some modifications using an LLM but I still tested these changes.

## Problem

ArtCraft creates its main webview with a fully transparent background (`Color(0, 0, 0, 0)`). Tauri forwards that color to WebKitGTK, so the webview surface has an alpha channel even though the app draws its own background.

On Fedora 43 / GNOME Wayland / NVIDIA, with the existing `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1` and `WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE=1` launcher defaults, the webview was mostly transparent: only the showcase video rendered, the login form was invisible, and the desktop showed through the window. Hovering repainted individual form fields.

This is the same symptom as #2294. The underlying NVIDIA explicit-sync crash is covered by open PRs #2031 and #2056 (and #1993 also sets `__NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC=1`). This PR is complementary: it removes the fragile transparent surface so unpainted regions show the app's background instead of the desktop. It does not replace those fixes.

## Change

- On Linux, create the webview with an opaque `#121316` background matching `--st-bg`.
- macOS and Windows keep the transparent background used by their window decorations.

## Related

- #2031 — Fix WebKitGTK rendering on NVIDIA Linux and focus the login form
- #2056 — Disable NVIDIA explicit sync for WebKitGTK on Linux
- #1993 — Linux: fix window sizing and NVIDIA crash, add build docs and publish workflow
- #2294 — Transparent UI Bug
- [WebKit bug 280210](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=280210)

## Verification

- `SQLX_OFFLINE=true cargo check -p artcraft` — passes (pre-existing warnings only)
- `node --test frontend/scripts/unix-dev.test.mjs` — 7/7 pass
- Launched on Fedora 43, GNOME Wayland, NVIDIA RTX 3090 (driver 580.178.04): the login form renders with the NVIDIA explicit-sync workaround applied.
- Not tested on macOS or Windows; those keep the previous transparent color.

title: frontend: lang/dir on the document and logical start/end styling for RTL
author: aiongg
body:
Groundwork for right-to-left interface languages in the web frontend, from the language-support plan in storytold/craft-libs#198 (track 8, N1). Nothing changes for English: the document stays `lang="en" dir="ltr"`.

**Document language**
- `setDocumentLanguage(tag, dir?)` in `@storyteller/common` sets `lang` and `dir` on `<html>`, deriving the direction from the tag (`Intl.Locale` text info, with a language/script list as fallback). The app calls it once at startup with the default `en`.

**Logical styling**
- 422 physical Tailwind classes become logical: `ml/mr` to `ms/me`, `pl/pr` to `ps/pe`, `left/right` to `start/end`, `text-left/right` to `text-start/end`, `rounded-l/r/*` to `rounded-s/e/*`, `border-l/r` to `border-s/e`. The 11 `space-x-*` rows get `rtl:space-x-reverse`.
- Transform origins next to converted positions, the switch thumbs and the prompt box resize grip get `rtl:` counterparts.
- Left physical on purpose: the 3D camera frame overlay, the video editor's timeline, preview and guides, the scene timeline and storyboard strip, `slider-v2`, the vector and number inputs, modal resize handles, media prev/next arrows (their chevrons and arrow keys don't mirror yet), the reference deck's fan, Radix sheet sides and tooltip arrows, the macOS traffic-light inset in the top bar, and every `left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2` centring. Inline `left:` styles are all measured coordinates and stay as they are.

**User text**
- Prompts, file names, model names, folder, board, tag, scene and character names get `dir="auto"` where they fill an element and `<bdi>` where they sit inside other text. Prompt textareas and the mention editor use `dir="auto"`.

**Related**
- #2216 adds an i18next-based `libs/i18n` and sets `document.documentElement.lang` on language change; with this PR it can call `setDocumentLanguage(language)` to set `dir` as well.

**Checks**
- `vite build` of the app passes, and the built CSS contains the logical and `rtl:` utilities.

title: frontend: craft-i18n catalogs, Noto fallback fonts and lang/dir for the i18n library
author: aiongg
body:
Builds on #2216 by @huchenlix (i18next in `frontend/libs/i18n`, English-keyed resources, the zh-CN interface) and #2519 (logical start/end CSS, `setDocumentLanguage`). This branch contains both; the last two commits are the change here. Part of the language-support plan in storytold/craft-libs#198 (item N1).

What it adds:

- **craft-i18n catalogs.** An i18next backend reads craft-i18n's TSV catalogs (`common.tsv` plus `artcraft.tsv` per locale), following craft-i18n's `docs/catalog-format.md`. Contexts map to i18next context keys, `@plural` rows to plural-suffixed keys used by a new `tn(t, n, one, other)`, and a broken row is skipped and logged so that string shows in English. Lookups go region, then language, then English. A `zh-hans` catalog fills the gaps in the bundled zh-CN.
- **Optional build input.** The `craftI18n` Vite plugin embeds every locale that has an `artcraft.tsv` when `CRAFT_I18N_DIR` is set, one lazy chunk per locale. Without it the build is English plus the bundled zh-CN, as today. `CRAFT_I18N_REQUIRED=1` makes a missing checkout an error. The language picker lists what is built in.
- **Fonts.** With `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR`, the `craftFonts` plugin copies craft-fonts' Noto faces (Arabic, Thai, CJK) and their licences to `craft-fonts/` in the build output and injects `@font-face` rules with each script's `unicode-range`, so a face downloads only when a character needs it. No font files are committed. The font stacks end in `var(--craft-fonts, sans-serif)`.
- **`lang` and `dir`.** Every language change calls `setDocumentLanguage`, so `dir="rtl"` follows an Arabic or Hebrew catalog and the start/end classes from #2519 apply.
- **First strings on catalog keys.** #2216's twelve semantic plural keys (`libraryFiles`, `creditCost`, …) become `tn()` calls with their English forms, which is what craft-i18n's `@plural` rows key on; the zh-CN entries are renamed to match. The top bar's upload button and scene title messages are translated.
